# **II. Requirement Specification** {#ii.-requirement-specification}

## ***II.1 Problem description*** {#ii.1-problem-description}

### *II.1.1 Background* {#ii.1.1-background}

During the 2024–2026 development phase, the Hoa Lac High-Tech and University Satellite Urban Area (Thach That and Quoc Oai districts, Hanoi) witnessed an unprecedented demographic expansion of over 45,000 to 50,000 young intellectuals, university students, and high-tech software engineers across major anchor institutions:

* **Vietnam National University, Hanoi (VNU) at Hoa Lac:** Currently hosts \~17,000 concentrated students across 11 member institutions, scaling to 30,000 by 2028 and 60,000 by 2030\.

* **FPT University (Hoa Lac Campus):** Educates and boards over 25,000 students on-campus full-time.

* **Hoa Lac High-Tech Park (HHTP):** Concentrates tens of thousands of R\&D engineers at FPT Software (Hola Park 1 & 2), Viettel High Tech, VNPT, Vingroup/VinAI, and Nidec.

Sedentary technical work has triggered an explosive surge in recreational sports, establishing Badminton (Cầu lông), Pickleball, and Table Tennis (Bóng bàn) as dominant community activities. Sports facilities face extreme saturation during golden hours (17:00–22:00 weekdays and all day on weekends).

An empirical field survey conducted across prominent venues—centered on the 368 Sports Complex (Cụm sân 368\) and neighboring facilities—revealed five critical operational breakdowns:

* **Ad-Hoc & Fragmented Booking:** Reservations are coordinated informally via Facebook student groups (FU \- Hoà Lạc \++, Chợ Hoà Lạc), private Zalo messages, or phone calls, with schedules hand-written in paper notebooks or spreadsheets.

* **Schedule Collisions & Double Bookings:** Without real-time concurrency controls, simultaneous inquiries routinely trigger 4 to 6 double-booking collisions per month during peak rush periods.

* **Pervasive No-Shows (Bùng sân):** Slot holds based on verbal trust or loose promises lead to an average 28% no-show rate. When customers fail to show up, venue operators cannot re-list the vacated slots in time, resulting in direct revenue forfeiture. 

* **Front-Desk Revenue Leakage:** Auxiliary retail (beverages, rental rackets, balls) and unrecorded overtime play depend on loose cash drawers, resulting in an estimated 18% revenue leakage without shift cash drawer audits.

* **Lack of Multi-Branch Governance:** Chain owners lack centralized oversight, leaving them with zero real-time visibility into branch court occupancy, cash drawer balances, and inventory discrepancies.

### *II.1.2 Business Opportunity* {#ii.1.2-business-opportunity}

#### ***II.1.2.1. Market Opportunity & Chain Scalability***

The booming demand across Hoa Lac presents an extraordinary opportunity for sports venue owners to deploy an automated, brand-owned, Multi-location, Single-owner Web Platform. Automating the entire operational lifecycle—from 24/7 public online booking to web-based counter check-in and shift reconciliation—enables venue chains to maximize court occupancy, eliminate cash leakage, and scale operations seamlessly across regional branches.

#### ***II.1.2.2. Analysis of Existing Market Solutions (Competitor Evaluation)***

An in-depth evaluation of current technological offerings reveals critical operational gaps that prevent them from satisfying the operational requirements of multi-sport facility chains:

* **Solution 1: PlaySpace System ([playspace.vn](http://playspace.vn)):** An All-in-One internal management ERP & POS software for sports facilities. While offering strong back-office scheduling, dynamic pricing, and inventory tracking, its fatal flaw is that it HAS NO PUBLIC CUSTOMER-FACING BOOKING PORTAL. Customers must still call or chat, and staff must manually input each booking. High licensing fees and complex interfaces impose heavy training overhead.

* **Solution 2: ALOBO Marketplace ([datlich.alobo.vn](http://datlich.alobo.vn)):** A multi-tenant aggregator marketplace. While providing public booking, GPS map discovery, and temporary slot holds (12–14m), its fatal flaw is aggregator dependency. It extracts a 5% to 12% commission per booking, siphons customer relationship data, exposes venue players to competing facilities on the map, and completely lacks back-office controls (no shift reconciliation, no Z-Report cash drawer audit, and no audited refund pipeline).

* **Solution 3: Ways Station ([waysstation.vn](http://waysstation.vn)):** A single-brand multi-branch booking website. While avoiding broker commissions, its fatal flaw is an oversimplified guest-only architecture. It provides no member accounts or loyalty profiles, NO ONLINE RECURRING BOOKING CAPABILITIES (teams must call hotlines to book monthly slots), flat static pricing (no peak/off-peak dynamic rules), and manual bank transfer screenshot verifications prone to order loss.

#### ***II.1.2.3. Competitive Solution Comparison Matrix***

Table 2 contrasts the operational capabilities of the three market alternatives against the proposed CourtChain platform:

| Operational Criterion | PlaySpace System | ALOBO Marketplace | Ways Station | CourtChain Platform |
| :---- | ----- | ----- | ----- | :---- |
| Public 24/7 Customer Booking Portal | No (Internal only) | Yes (Shared marketplace) | Yes (Brand website) | Yes (100% Brand-Owned Web Portal) |
| Marketplace Booking Commission Fee | 0% (Software fee) | 5% – 12% / booking | 0% | 0% (Direct Revenue) |
| Customer Data Ownership | Yes (Private) | No (Siphoned by platform) | Yes (Private) | Yes (100% Venue Chain Ownership) |
| Real-Time Concurrency Lock (Anti-Collision) | No (Manual entry) | Moderate (12–14m basic lock) | Moderate (Basic lock) | Yes (Redis Distributed Lock TTL 7m) |
| Online Recurring Booking Subscriptions | No (Manual entry) | No | No (Phone hotline only) | Yes (Self-service 4–12 week subscriptions) |
| Web Counter POS & Stock Auto-Deduction | Yes (Comprehensive) | No | No | Yes (Browser POS \+ Auto Stock Deduction) |
| Dedicated Hardware Requirement | Yes (PC/POS hardware) | No | No | Yes (Zero dedicated POS hardware; web-only) |
| Cash Drawer Z-Report & Dual Shift Sign-Off | Moderate (General cashbook) | No | No | Yes (Mandatory physical count & dual approval) |
| Audited Bank Refund via Napas247 VietQR | No | Moderate (Platform wallet/card) | No (No refunds) | Yes (Dynamic VietQR \+ Mandatory bill upload) |
| Centralized Multi-Branch Governance | Moderate (Branch switcher) | No (Marketplace) | Moderate (Basic) | Yes (Multi-location Single-owner Architecture) |

 

#### ***II.1.2.4. The CourtChain Strategic Advantage***

* **Zero Broker Fees & Permanent Data Ownership:** 100% of revenue flows directly to the owner without third-party commission deductions, while permanently retaining customer relationship data.

* **Distributed Concurrency Lock (Redis TTL 420s):** Eliminates 100% of double bookings and slot hoarding during golden hour checkout rushes.

* **100% Web-Based Counter Operations:** Eliminates expensive POS hardware by running directly in standard web browsers using USB barcode scanners or webcams.

* **Dual-Approved Z-Report Shift Reconciliation:** Enforces physical cash counts, automated variance formulas, and manager sign-off to eliminate cash drawer leakage.

* **Audited Direct Bank Refund Pipeline:** Replaces untrusted virtual wallets with automated dynamic VietQR codes (Napas247) and mandatory bank receipt archiving.

### *II.1.3 Business Objectives (BO)* {#ii.1.3-business-objectives-(bo)}

***BO-1: Eliminate Schedule Collisions and Minimize No-Show Rates***

* **Statement:** Eliminate 100% of double-booking incidents and reduce customer no-shows from \~28% to under 3% across all chain facilities within 3 months of launch.  
* **Scale:** Percentage of reserved court hours resulting in unfulfilled no-shows; monthly count of double-booking conflicts.  
* **Meter:** Automated operational audit logs from CourtChain Reservation Analytics.  
* **Past (Baseline):** Instances of non-arrival after booking occur  
* **Goal:** No-show rate \< 3.0%; Double-booking incidents \= 0\.  
* **Stretch Goal:** No-show rate \< 1.0%; Double-booking incidents \= 0 (absolute elimination).

***BO-2: Maximize Court Utilization Efficiency and Accelerate Chain Revenue***

* **Statement:** Increase off-peak court occupancy by at least 20% and grow total net chain revenue by 25% within 6 months post-launch through dynamic pricing and real-time public slot availability.

* **Scale:** Facility court utilization rate (utilized court hours / available operating hours); total monthly net revenue.

* **Meter:** Chain-wide P\&L and utilization reports (/mn\_ground\_report) on the Court Owner Executive Dashboard.

* **Past (Baseline):** 52% average occupancy (heavy congestion 18:00–21:00; mornings and early afternoons largely vacant).

* **Goal:** Overall chain occupancy rate \>= 72%; Net revenue growth \>= 25% within 6 months.

* **Stretch Goal:** Overall chain occupancy rate \>= 80%; Net revenue growth \>= 35%.

***BO-3: Eliminate Front-Desk Financial Discrepancies and Auxiliary Service Leakage***

* **Statement:** Reduce auxiliary retail inventory and cash discrepancies from \~18% to under 1.0% by enforcing real-time POS inventory auto-deduction and mandatory dual-signed Z-Report shift closings.

* **Scale:** Percentage difference between physical cash counted in drawer versus expected system revenue; stock loss discrepancy rate.

* **Meter:** Periodic physical stocktaking logs (/stocktaking) and electronic Z-Report shift-closing summaries (/shift-closing).

* **Past (Baseline):** There is loss in auxiliary beverage/equipment sales due to unrecorded cash transactions and lack of shift handover protocols.

* **Goal:** Cash drawer discrepancy \< 1.0%; Inventory loss rate \< 1.0%.

* **Stretch Goal:** Cash drawer discrepancy \< 0.2%; Inventory loss rate \< 0.2%.

***BO-4: Automate Booking Processing and Eliminate Third-Party Broker Commissions***

* **Statement:** Automate 100% of the customer booking and payment workflow, saving 100% of marketplace commission fees and reducing staff hours spent answering manual scheduling inquiries by over 80%.

* **Scale:** Third-party marketplace commission fees paid; daily staff hours dedicated to manual chat/call schedule coordination.

* **Meter:** Financial operating expense balance sheets and shift task duration logs.

* **Past (Baseline):** 3 to 5 staff hours per day spent answering booking chats; 8% to 10% commission fees incurred if listing on marketplace platforms.

* **Goal:** Third-party commission fees \= 0 VND (100% direct revenue); Staff scheduling coordination time reduced by \>= 80%.

* **Stretch Goal:** 100% autonomous 24/7 online booking execution with zero staff intervention required for reservations.

### *II.1.4 Success Metrics (SM)* {#ii.1.4-success-metrics-(sm)}

The operational deployment will be evaluated against five quantitative success metrics:

* **SM-1 (Online Self-Service Adoption Rate):** Within 3 months of launch, at least 80% of all single-court bookings across the chain are transacted entirely through the self-service Web Booking Portal without staff phone or chat intervention.

* **SM-2 (Customer Retention & Repeat Rate):** At least 65% of registered customers who complete an initial booking make a subsequent reservation or enroll in a recurring booking plan within 60 days.

* **SM-3 (Front-Desk Check-In Processing Speed):** Counter reception throughput achieves an average processing time of \< 5 seconds per customer for QR code scans and \< 15 seconds per customer for phone number or Booking ID lookups.

* **SM-4 (Shift Handover Audit Compliance):** 100% of front-desk shifts execute the standardized Z-Report electronic closing workflow with physical cash verification prior to shift handover.

* **SM-5 (Instant Cancellation Slot De-Allocation Latency):** 100% of approved cancellations release their vacated court slots back to the public booking grid in \< 1 second, enabling at least 40% of vacated slots to be successfully resold.

### *II.1.5 Vision Statement* {#ii.1.5-vision-statement}

| COURTCHAIN VISION STATEMENTFor: *Sports venue chain owners (such as 368 Sports Complex in Hoa Lac) and the community of students, lecturers, and high-tech software engineers who play Badminton, Pickleball, and Table Tennis;* Who: *Require a transparent, 24/7 online court booking platform and an automated back-office operations system to eliminate double bookings, no-shows, and front-desk revenue leakage;* The CourtChain: *Is an enterprise-grade, cloud-based Multi-Sport Court Chain Booking & Facility Operation Management Web Platform operating under a Multi-location, Single-owner architecture;* That: *Provides an exclusive brand-owned booking portal with real-time schedule grids, distributed 7-minute concurrency holding locks (Redis TTL), 100% online prepayment via VNPay, ultra-fast check-in (\<5s), web-based front-desk POS with inventory auto-deduction, mandatory shift-closing Z-Reports, and audited direct bank refunds via dynamic VietQR (Napas247);* Unlike: *Third-party broker marketplaces (such as ALOBO) that charge 5%–12% commission fees, poach customer relationships, and lack back-office controls; internal ERP tools (such as PlaySpace) that lack a public customer-facing booking portal; or barebones venue websites (such as Ways Station) that lack member profiles and recurring booking capabilities;* Our Product: *Empowers facility chain owners to retain 100% of their booking revenue, permanently own their customer data, maximize court occupancy, and professionalize chain operations across all sports facilities at Hoa Lac.* |

### *II.1.6 Business Risks (RI)* {#ii.1.6-business-risks-(ri)}

| Risk ID | Business Risk Description | Prob (P) | Impact (I) | Score (P\*I) | Mitigation & Prevention Strategy |
| :---: | :---- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---- |
| RI-1 | User Inertia & Habitual Manual Booking: Students continue messaging Zalo or calling venue staff rather than using the web portal. | 0.5 | 6 | 3.0 | Implement promotional incentives (5%–10% web discounts, complimentary beverage vouchers); place prominent QR scan stands at physical courts for instant on-site web onboarding. |
| RI-2 | Third-Party Payment Gateway Downtime: Outages or network timeouts on VNPay disrupt online checkout. | 0.3 | 8 | 2.4 | Implement an automated fallback: if VNPay API times out, the system generates a dynamic VietQR code tied directly to the facility bank account with an embedded order reference for instant Napas247 transfer. |
| RI-3 | Front-Desk POS Under-Reporting Fraud: Cashiers bypass the web POS to sell beverages or rent equipment for personal cash gain. | 0.4 | 7 | 2.8 | Position surveillance cameras directly above the beverage coolers and front desk; enforce mandatory weekly physical inventory counts; apply penalty clauses and performance sales bonuses. |
| RI-4 | Peak-Hour Concurrency Surges: Sudden spikes in web traffic when prime-time weekend slots open overload backend servers. | 0.3 | 7 | 2.1 | Deploy Redis connection pooling, database query optimization with composite indexing on (court\_id, start\_time), and cloud container auto-scaling. |
| RI-5 | Policy Exploitation & Speculative Cancellations: Customers hold slots and cancel at the last minute to manipulate availability. | 0.4 | 6 | 2.4 | Enforce a strict tiered refund policy (\>=24h: 80% refund; 12–24h: 50% refund; 6–12h: 0% refund, reschedule only; \<2h: strict lock); limit member accounts to a maximum of 2 cancellations per month. |

 

### *II.1.7 Business Assumptions & Dependencies (AS & DE)* {#ii.1.7-business-assumptions-&-dependencies-(as-&-de)}

#### ***1\. Business Assumptions (AS)***

* **AS-1 (Technological Accessibility):** 100% of target users (university students, university staff, IT engineers in Hoa Lac) possess smartphones with 4G/Wifi connectivity and active mobile banking applications capable of scanning VNPay/VietQR codes.

* **AS-2 (Staff Operational Discipline):** Front-desk personnel receive comprehensive training and adhere strictly to web-based check-in verification and end-of-shift Z-Report reconciliation procedures.

* **AS-3 (Supply Chain Continuity):** Beverage distributors, equipment suppliers (rackets, balls, shuttlecocks) maintain stable delivery schedules to each branch facility.

* **AS-4 (Regulatory & Banking Compliance):** Direct refund transfers via Napas247 dynamic VietQR are recognized as legitimate corporate commercial transactions under Vietnamese banking laws, avoiding the regulatory hazards of unapproved virtual wallet systems.

#### ***2\. Business Dependencies (DE)***

* **DE-1 (Payment Gateway Infrastructure):** System checkout depends on the continuous operational availability of the VNPay Payment Gateway API and Instant Payment Notification (IPN) webhooks.

* **DE-2 (Transactional Email Delivery Service):** Automated dispatch of booking confirmations, QR check-in tickets, and guest cancellation tokens depends on reliable 3rd-party SMTP/API services (SendGrid).

* **DE-3 (On-Site Network Infrastructure):** Branch reception counters must maintain high-speed broadband connections and localized Wi-Fi to support continuous web POS operations and QR scanning without latency.

## ***II.2 Major Features*** {#ii.2-major-features}

| ID | Name | Description |
| :---: | :---- | :---- |
| **MF1** | **Court Booking Services** | Provides comprehensive self-service sports court discovery and booking for guests and members: multi-sport facility search (badminton, pickleball, table tennis), interactive schedule grid with real-time slot availability, 7-minute distributed temporary hold locks (TTL) preventing double bookings, single-session and recurring subscription bookings (4–12 weeks), promotional voucher discount redemption, 100% online prepayment via VNPay, automated QR e-ticket delivery, pre-visit equipment/service preferences, and verified post-play court reviews. |
| **MF2** | **Booking Lifecycle Management** | Governs the complete post-booking operational lifecycle: viewing booking history and real-time status tracking, self-service single session rescheduling (\>= 2h cutoff) and manager-assisted emergency rescheduling, recurring absence reporting with automatic make-up session entitlement tracking (valid within 30 days), structured tiered cancellation policies (\>=24h: 80%, 12–24h: 50%, 6–12h: 30%, \<6h: 0%), immediate reopening of cancelled slots, tiered refund authorization (Facility Manager up to 1,000,000 VND; Court Owner for higher amounts), and audited multi-channel refund disbursements (VNPay online refund, bank transfer with audit slips, or counter cash). |
| **MF3** | **Front-Desk Operations** | Equips front-desk staff to deliver fast on-site customer service: creating direct walk-in court bookings, checking in customers via mobile web camera QR scanning or reference code lookup, managing active session extensions, processing counter sales of beverages and consumable sports items with real-time stock deduction, registering sports equipment rentals with required deposit recording, inspecting returned rental gear and assessing damage compensation fees, calculating tiered overtime charges, and executing counter invoice settlements with printed receipts. |
| **MF4** | **Shift Reconciliation** | Enforces strict financial control and cash drawer accountability across employee shifts: declaring opening cash float at shift start, recording all shift cash and online payment events tagged to the active shift, categorizing transactions across payment channels (cash, bank transfer, VNPay), performing mandatory physical cash denomination counting at closing, generating discrepancy reports for cash shortages or overages, and creating immutable shift handover Z-Reports requiring facility manager review and sign-off. |
| **MF5** | **Facility Operations Management** | Supports facility managers in running daily branch operations: toggling court maintenance locks to block damaged courts, resolving affected customer bookings through compensation or rebooking, managing branch retail and equipment stock (supplier goods receipt verification, periodic inventory stocktaking, stock variance adjustments, and low-stock alerts), provisioning and deactivating staff user accounts, scheduling employee shift rosters, and monitoring branch court occupancy metrics and revenue summaries. |
| **MF6** | **Chain Administration** | Centralizes strategic chain-wide governance for the Court Owner: registering and updating branch facilities, configuring multi-sport court assets, defining flexible court rental pricing matrices across regular/peak hours and weekends, establishing promotional voucher discount campaigns, appointing and managing facility managers, maintaining master inventory SKU catalogs with branch-specific selling prices and hourly rental rates, approving inter-branch stock transfer requests, and analyzing consolidated chain-wide occupancy, inventory, and financial dashboards. |
| **MF7** | **Identity Management** | Secures platform authentication and user identity management: member account registration with credential validation, secure password authentication, federated Google OAuth single sign-on, email-based password recovery, profile information maintenance, password changes, and enforcement of granular role-based access control (RBAC) and facility-scoped data boundaries across all system capabilities. |

## II.4 Nonfunctional requirements  {#ii.4-nonfunctional-requirements}

| \# | Non-Functional Requirement | Description | Detailed Specification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Performance** | Optimize transaction processing, real-time availability rendering, and operational response times across all customer and staff touchpoints. | • **Customer & Guest:** Real-time court availability matrix and schedule loading must complete in \< 2.0 seconds under peak traffic; slot reservation hold lock must execute in \< 1.0 second; VNPay payment redirection must initiate in \< 1.5 seconds; automated booking confirmation email with attached QR e-ticket must be dispatched via SendGrid within \< 15.0 seconds. • **Front-Desk Staff (Cashier):** Mobile web QR code check-in verification using a smartphone camera must complete in \< 1.0 second; booking lookup by phone number or 6-character booking code must render within \< 2.0 seconds; dynamic VietQR generation for counter payments must render in \< 2.0 seconds; POS session check-out, service adjustments, and physical receipt printing must execute in \< 1.5 seconds. • **Facility Manager:** Shift reconciliation summaries, cash variance calculations, and Z-Report approval rendering must complete in \< 3.0 seconds; branch inventory stocktake records and goods receipt processing  must be processed and saved to the database within \< 2.0 seconds. • **Court Owner:** Aggregated multi-branch financial reports and chain-wide court occupancy analytics must render within \< 3.0 seconds; bulk court pricing policy updates and promotional voucher campaign creations must save within \< 2.0 seconds. • **Slot Resale Latency:** Released court slots resulting from approved cancellations, member rescheduling, or expired temporary holds must be restored to the availability matrix and become available for immediate resale to other customers in \< 1.0 second. |
| **2** | **Scalability** | Ensure capacity expansion, sustained throughput, and multi-branch horizontal growth. | • **Concurrency:** The system must seamlessly support at least 200 concurrent user sessions without exceeding performance latency thresholds. • **Data Volume:** The relational database must be capable of storing at least 500,000 booking sessions, 200,000 invoices, 50,000 customer accounts, 5,000 inventory items, and 3 years of historical financial logs without degrading query response times by more than 10%. • **Multi-Branch Expansion (Horizontal Scalability):** The architectural framework and database tenancy model must support scaling up to 20 branch facilities, 200 courts, and 50 POS counters across the chain with zero schema restructuring or architectural redesign. • **Traffic Surge Absorption:** Redis distributed caching and connection pooling must absorb sudden traffic spikes during promotional voucher campaign launches and holiday reservation openings without causing thread pool exhaustion or database query timeouts. |
| **3** | **Security** | Protect sensitive user and financial data, enforce strict access boundaries, and maintain tamper-proof audit trails. | • **Authentication & Session Management:** Passwords must be encrypted using industry-standard hashing algorithms and never logged in plain text; Google OAuth 2.0 SSO identity tokens must be verified server-side and strictly assigned to the Customer role. Stateless JWT access tokens expire after 60 minutes, paired with a 7-day refresh token rotation. Front-desk Staff POS sessions must automatically lock upon shift closure or cash handover; Facility Manager and Owner administrative sessions must automatically time out after 30 minutes of inactivity. Guest cancellation requests must use HMAC-SHA256 cryptographically signed, single-use magic links that expire immediately at session start time. • **Access Control & Multi-Tenant Data Isolation:** The system shall implement strict 4-tier Role-Based Access Control. Warehouse and inventory management must be strictly segregated from front-desk staff. Enforce rigorous multi-branch data isolation at the middleware/repository layer—Staff and Facility Managers are strictly quarantined to their assigned facility ID, completely denying access to sales revenue, pricing configurations, or records belonging to other branches. • **Payment Security & Communications:** 100% of network traffic must be encrypted over HTTPS / TLS 1.3. No credit card, bank account credentials, or Google passwords are stored in the local database. All incoming VNPay IPN webhooks must be authenticated using SHA512 HMAC checksum verification to prevent request tampering or spoofing. • **Financial Auditing & Immutability:** 100% of critical operational and financial events must be immutably recorded in audit logs with User ID, Facility ID, exact timestamp, and client IP/device. Approved shift Z-Reports and completed refund records are strictly read-only and permanently locked against modification or deletion. Staff must provide an explanation of at least 20 characters for any shift cash variance. |
| **4** | **Reliability & Availability** | Ensure continuous operational uptime, atomic concurrency control, and robust fault tolerance. | • **Availability:** The system must achieve at least 99.5% operational uptime during business operating hours (06:00 to 23:00 daily), with planned maintenance restricted to off-peak night windows (23:30–05:30) with prior user notification banners. • **Concurrency Control & Race Condition Prevention:** High-contention court slot bookings must be governed by Redis atomic distributed locks with a strictly enforced 7-minute Time-To-Live (TTL) hold window. A secondary database-level composite unique constraint must guarantee zero double-booking even during cache failures or network partitions. • **Payment Webhook Idempotency & Fault Tolerance:** VNPay payment confirmation webhooks must be strictly idempotent using unique transaction references to guarantee that duplicate gateway callbacks cannot result in multiple charges or duplicate bookings. Late payments arriving after a hold expires must be automatically flagged for reconciliation/refund without resurrecting expired holds or overriding newly booked slots. • **Automated Background Job Reliability:** Background cron workers must execute idempotently with automatic retry mechanisms and error logging. Reminders for pending refunds or shift reports exceeding 24 hours must automatically escalate to the Facility Manager, and to the Court Owner after 48 hours. • **Disaster Recovery & Data Resilience:** Automated daily full database backups with continuous Write-Ahead Log (WAL) archiving must ensure a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of \< 15 minutes and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of \< 2 hours in the event of hardware or server failure. |
| **5** | **Usability & Operability** | Maximize front-desk operational efficiency and streamline customer booking workflows. | • **Customer Self-Service Interface:** Intuitive 3-step online booking flow, fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers; clear real-time color-coded visual slot status indicators; real-time countdown timer for the 7-minute payment hold. • **Front-Desk Mobile & Web Operability:** Staff POS interface optimized for high-speed counter operations; supports direct smartphone camera QR code scanning without dedicated hardware, single-click search by phone number or 6-character booking code, and one-touch receipt generation with ESC/POS printer support. • **Error Prevention & Operational Fallback:** The UI must display human-readable, non-technical error notifications within \< 500 ms when slots are contested or holds expire. If dynamic VietQR generation fails due to gateway latency, the system must immediately provide a manual bank transfer fallback displaying account number, bank name, transfer syntax, and exact amount. |
| **6** | **Maintainability & Portability** | Ensure modular system architecture, cross-platform compatibility, and peripheral interoperability. | • **Modular Layered Architecture:** Clean separation of concerns adhering to SOLID principles, enabling independent updates, automated unit testing, and seamless replacement of third-party services . • **Cross-Platform Compatibility:** Fully compatible and visually consistent across all major modern web browsers on desktop  and mobile devices without requiring proprietary plugins. • **Hardware & Peripheral Interoperability:** Front-desk operations must support standard 80mm/58mm thermal receipt printers via browser print interfaces, and standard mobile device cameras for barcode/QR scanning via HTML5 WebRTC APIs without requiring dedicated native mobile apps. |

## II.5 Functional requirements {#ii.5-functional-requirements}

### II.5*.1 Actors* {#ii.5.1-actors}

| \# | Actor | Description |
| :---: | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Guest** | Anonymous visitor without an account. Can browse facility directories, search courts, view real-time availability grids, book single court sessions with a 7-minute payment hold, pay online via VNPay, submit advance preparation preferences, request cancellations via secure email link, and register for a member account. Cannot book recurring sessions, use member vouchers, or post reviews. |
| **2** | **Customer** | Registered member with an active account. Holds all Guest booking capabilities, plus exclusive privileges: creating 4–12 week recurring booking contracts, applying promotional discount vouchers, accessing personal booking history, self-service rescheduling of single sessions, reporting absences and redeeming make-up slots within 30 days, requesting cancellations under tiered refund policies, submitting post-visit ratings and reviews, and managing profile details. |
| **3** | **Staff** | On-site front-desk operator assigned to a specific branch. Opens and closes work shifts with cash float declarations, uses a smartphone camera via mobile web browser to scan ticket QR codes (or looks up booking codes/phone numbers) for court check-in, creates walk-in reservations, adjusts active court sessions and extensions, sells retail consumables, registers sports gear rentals with deposit tracking, assesses equipment damage fees, calculates tiered overtime surcharges, and collects counter payments with printed receipts. |
| **4** | **Facility Manager** | Branch-level operations manager holding all Staff operational privileges. Approves booking cancellations and audited refunds within facility thresholds (cumulative up to 1,000,000 VND per booking), audits and approves shift handover Z-Reports, creates and manages staff user accounts, schedules employee shifts, toggles court maintenance blocks and resolves affected customer bookings, oversees branch retail and rental equipment inventory (goods receipts, stocktaking, adjustments), and requests or receives inter-branch stock transfers. |
| **5** | **Court Owner** | Chain-wide executive and platform administrator. Configures facilities, multi-sport courts, and branch profiles; defines hourly court rental pricing policies across regular and peak hours; designs promotional voucher campaigns; appoints and revokes facility managers; maintains master SKU inventory catalogs with branch-specific selling prices and hourly rental rates; approves escalated refunds (\> 1,000,000 VND) and bank transfer refund slips; decides inter-branch stock transfers; and monitors consolidated executive analytics and financial reports. |
| **6** | **VNPay** | External payment gateway supporting system. Processes 100% online prepayments for court booking checkout flows via domestic bank cards, QR codes, and e-wallets, and executes automated online refund transactions back to original customer payment sources upon authorized approval. |
| **7** | **Email Service** | External notification supporting system. Delivers automated transactional emails generated by CourtChain, including booking confirmation summaries with attached QR e-tickets, guest cancellation management links, refund approval/rejection audit notices, and password reset verification links. |
| **8** | **Google Maps** | External digital mapping service. Supplies interactive geographic maps, branch location coordinates, visual pin markers, and direct navigation routes for guests and customers discovering facility venues. |
| **9** | **Google OAuth** | External federated authentication provider. Verifies customer identity via Google single sign-on (SSO), allowing quick member login without storing separate passwords (restricted strictly to the Customer role without granting internal staff/manager permissions). |
| **10** | **Receipt Printer** | Hardware peripheral connected to the front-desk workstation. Receives print commands directly from the CourtChain web application to produce physical paper receipts for walk-in bookings, retail sales, equipment rental deposits, overtime fees, and shift closing reports. |

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **Primary Actor:** | Guest, Customer | **Secondary Actors:** | Payment Gateway (VNPay), Email Service (SendGrid) |
| **Trigger:** | The user selects available court/time periods at one facility on one playing date and clicks "Book Now". |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: One facility and one date per order. PRE-2: All selected sessions satisfy BR1\-6. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: One Booking contains the selected BookingSessions and contact snapshot. POST-2: Checkout holds all selected periods for 420 seconds. POST-3: Successful settlement within the hold confirms all sessions and issues their check-in passes. Expiry releases unconfirmed holds. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The user selects one facility, one playing date, and one or more courts and time periods. 2\. The System validates each session and displays the order, per-session prices and total. 3\. The user enters the order contact name, phone and email; these are saved as a snapshot. 4\. The user may add session-specific preparation preferences through UC8; they do not increase the online court fee. 5\. A Customer may apply a voucher through UC6. Before checkout, its value is provisional. 6\. The user reviews all sessions, discount allocation and amount due, then selects "Proceed to Payment". 7\. The System rechecks all selected periods and voucher eligibility, then holds the complete selection and applicable voucher for the same 420-second period. A conflict leaves no partial order hold. 8\. Create Booking \= PendingPayment and sessions \= Planned, reservationStatus \= Holding. 9\. If amount due is positive, invoke UC7. If zero, confirm the zero-due settlement without a VNPay charge while the hold remains valid. 10\. On confirmation, set Booking \= Confirmed and all selected reservations \= Booked; consume the held voucher once, if any. 11\. Send an order confirmation with the individual session details and check-in passes. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | AF-1 Voucher: At Step 5, a logged-in Customer invokes UC6. Guest bookings cannot apply vouchers. AF-2 Zero Amount Due: At Step 9, confirm within the valid hold without invoking UC7 or creating a successful gateway payment record. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Slot or Voucher Conflict: Recheck the entire selection; retain no partial checkout hold and request revision. EX-2 Payment Failure: Allow retry while the original hold remains valid. EX-3 Hold Expired: Mark the unconfirmed booking Expired and its held sessions Cancelled; release their holds and any held voucher. Late successful payment follows UC7. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~300 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Session eligibility and checkout hold: BR1, BR2, BR3, BR4, BR5, BR6, BR7, BR8, BR9, BR10, BR25. Contact and preferences: BR11, BR12, BR13, BR14, BR15. Voucher eligibility and calculation: BR28, BR29, BR30, BR31, BR32, BR33, BR34, BR35, BR36, BR37, BR38, BR39, BR50, BR51, BR63, BR65, BR66. Committed price: BR40, BR62. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Concurrency lock implemented using Redlock algorithm to eliminate 100% of double bookings. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | VNPay payment gateway operates continuously without prolonged outages. |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The user is authenticated with role CUSTOMER (BR16). PRE-2: All requested recurring slots across all future dates in the series are available or resolvable. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: A recurring contract and its dated sessions are recorded under one Booking. POST-2: Settlement of the first amount due within the hold activates the contract and confirms all generated sessions. POST-3: Later installments remain payable; Booked does not mean every session is paid. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The Customer selects facility, sport, courts, weekdays, times, startDate and endDate. Validate BR17\-19 and BR43. 2\. Generate dated sessions for the 4-12 consecutive-week range. 3\. Show conflicts with reservations, holds and maintenance. 4\. Resolve each conflict by an allowed court/time change or omission; omitted occurrences are not charged (BR44/45/54/55). 5\. Show the finalized sessions and 4-week installment amounts. Allow session-specific preferences through UC8 and an eligible first-cycle voucher through UC6. 6\. The Customer reviews the first amount due and proceeds to checkout. 7\. Create the Booking and contract as PendingPayment; sessions are Planned with Holding reservations. On settlement within the hold, set the contract Active, Booking Confirmed and all generated reservations Booked. Consume the held voucher once. 10\. Keep later 4-week installments as separate obligations. Booked sessions still require full payment before check-in (BR58/59). 11\. Send the contract schedule and session passes. Later overdue cycles follow BR46\-48; do not apply the checkout expiry to an already confirmed series. |  |  |

AF-2 Apply Recurring Voucher: 1\. At Step 5, Customer enters a promo voucher valid for recurring contracts (BR64). 2\. The System invokes UC6 — Apply Voucher to deduct discount before checkout. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Checkout Conflict: If any generated session is no longer available, do not retain a partial series hold; return to conflict resolution. EX-2 Payment Failure: Keep the original hold until its expiry so the customer can retry. EX-3 Hold Expiry: Mark the pending contract and Booking Expired, cancel unconfirmed sessions and release their holds and any held voucher. Preserve payment history; handle late payments through UC7. |  |  |

| **Frequency of Use:** | \~20 times / day |  |  |

Availability and pricing: BR6, BR25, BR40, BR50, BR51, BR62. First-cycle voucher: BR28, BR29, BR30, BR31, BR32, BR33, BR34, BR35, BR36, BR37, BR38, BR39, BR63, BR64, BR65, BR66. Late payment: BR60, BR61. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | The 420-second hold applies to checkout only. Confirmed series follow installment rules. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The Customer commits to an ongoing sports schedule. |  |  |

**7 \<\<UC7 Pay Online\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC7 Pay Online |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | AnhTNHE181857 | **Date Created:** | 9/27/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Guest, Customer | **Secondary Actors:** | Payment Gateway (VNPay), Email Service (SendGrid) |
| **Trigger:** | Invoked by UC4, UC5, UC12, UC14 or UC16 when a positive online payment is due and the target reservation hold is valid. |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a paying booker, I want to complete 100% online prepayment through VNPay, so that my reserved court slot is confirmed and guaranteed. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: Court slot(s) are locked in HOLDING state with active 420-second (7-minute) TTL (BR5). PRE-2: Total payable amount is calculated and greater than 0\. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The verified payment result is recorded once. POST-2: A successful payment within the valid hold enables the calling UC to confirm its booking or change. POST-3: Late payment does not restore expired holds and enters refund handling. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Record the amount due and the originating booking or change request; create a VNPay payment request. 2\. Redirect the user to VNPay. 3\. The user chooses a supported payment method and authorizes payment. 4\. Receive and validate the gateway callback, transaction reference, amount and result. 5\. Record the payment result once; repeated callbacks must not duplicate confirmation, collection or voucher consumption. 6\. Before confirming, recheck the target hold and the originating request. 7\. If the payment succeeds while eligible, return settlement success to that UC to confirm the booking or apply the change. Do not release an old reservation on payment success alone. 8\. If the hold expired, keep the payment record and initiate the late-payment refund process without restoring expired reservations. 9\. Display the verified outcome; send the confirmed session details only after successful booking/change confirmation. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Payment Cancelled or Failed: Display the result and allow retry before the original hold expires. EX-2 Invalid Callback: Reject it; do not confirm a booking or change. EX-3 Late Successful Payment: Preserve the payment; refund it in full under BR60. The Manager reconciles within 24 hours and initiates refund processing within 48 hours of receipt verification (BR61). EX-4 Duplicate Callback: Return the recorded outcome without repeating business effects. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~320 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Hold and payment confirmation: BR5, BR7, BR9, BR10. Late payment handling: BR60, BR61. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | End-to-end communication secured via HTTPS / TLS 1.3 with SHA-256 HMAC signature. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | VNPay payment gateway and banking switch networks are operational. |  |  |

**11 \<\<UC11 Find Booking Record\>\>**  
***UC11 — Find Booking Record***

| UC ID and Name: | UC11 Find Booking Record |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | MinhHT | **Date Created:** | 21/10/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Staff, Facility Manager, Court Owner | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | An internal operator (Staff, Facility Manager, or Court Owner) accesses the booking management console to search and inspect specific customer court booking records. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Enables staff, facility managers, and the court owner to search, filter, and inspect detailed booking records by customer phone number, booking code, customer name, date range, payment status, and booking status within their assigned operational authorization scope. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1:** The actor is logged in with valid Staff, Facility Manager, or Court Owner role privileges (BR250). **PRE-2:** The actor has assigned operational scope (Staff/Manager restricted to assigned branch; Court Owner has chain-wide scope). |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1:** Matching booking records meeting search criteria are retrieved and rendered with summary cards and tabular metrics. **POST-2:** If a specific booking is selected, comprehensive reservation details (court, time slot, pricing, applied vouchers, service orders, payments, audit history) are displayed. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\.** The actor navigates to the "Booking Management" module and selects "Find Booking Record". **2\.** The System retrieves the actor's authorization scope and displays search filters (Customer Phone, Booking Code, Date Range, Court, Status: Reserved / Confirmed / Checked-in / Completed / Cancelled, Payment Status). **3\.** The actor enters one or more search criteria and clicks "Search Bookings". **4\.** The System validates the input parameters and queries the booking repository, applying branch scope restrictions. **5\.** The System displays a paginated list of matching booking records showing Booking Code, Customer Name & Phone, Court Name, Scheduled Time, Total Amount, and Current Status. **6\.** The actor clicks on a booking record to inspect complete details. **7\.** The System retrieves and renders the booking aggregate modal: session schedule, court assignment, invoice details, check-in timestamp, service add-ons, and audit trail. |  |  |

The System displays: "No booking records found matching your search parameters." **EX-2 Invalid Input Format:** 1\. The phone number contains invalid characters or booking code format is malformed. 2\. The System highlights the invalid field and displays an error prompt. |  |  |

| **Other Information:** | Staff view is strictly bounded to the local facility; Court Owner can toggle search across all chain branches. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Historical booking records and completed sessions are retained and indexed in the persistent database. |  |  |

**12 \<\<UC12 Reschedule Single Session\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC12 Reschedule Single Session |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | AnhTNHE181857 | **Date Created:** | 10/3/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Customer | **Secondary Actors:** | Payment Gateway (VNPay), Email Service (SendGrid) |
| **Trigger:** | The Customer clicks "Reschedule Booking / Change Slot" on an upcoming reservation in Booking History. |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a Customer with a single reservation, I want to reschedule to another time slot or court when my schedule changes, avoiding cancellation and settling price differences transparently. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The Customer owns the selected Planned, Booked single-booking session. PRE-2: At least 2 hours remain before its start (BR79/112). PRE-3: Its one permitted reschedule has not been used (BR105, session scope). |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: After a successful change, release the original reservation. Reopen its period only if no other active hold, reservation or maintenance block remains (BR8). POST-2: Confirm the replacement period under the same Booking and preserve session history. POST-3: Issue and email an updated session pass. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Select the session to change within its Booking. 2\. Check ownership, at least 2 hours' notice and the unused one-change allowance. 3\. Display available periods at the same facility, same sport and duration, within 14 calendar days of the request (BR113). 4\. Select a new court/time. Check the order's common playing-date constraint when it contains other sessions. 5\. Calculate max(new standard fee \- old post-voucher fee, 0); do not apply a new voucher or refund a cheaper choice. 6\. Recheck and temporarily hold the target period while retaining the original reservation. 7\. If a supplement is due, invoke UC7; otherwise proceed without a gateway payment. 8\. Revalidate the change, confirm the new period and release the old reservation together. Only then record the successful change and update the session's schedule. 9\. Keep history and issue an updated pass. On failure or expiry, retain the original session and release only the replacement hold. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Under 2 Hours: Reject self-service change under BR79/112; an assisted request may be reviewed under BR111 and BR157, without guaranteed approval. EX-2 Conflict, Payment Failure or Expired Target Hold: Do not release the original session or consume its change allowance. EX-3 Limit or Target Rules Failed: Reject an already-used allowance or an invalid facility, sport, duration, horizon or order date. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~25 times / day |  |  |

POST-2: One linked make-up entitlement is available until the end of original session date \+ 30 calendar days. POST-3: Reserve one shared allowance for that original month; no cash refund is created. |  |  |

Check one shared allowance per contract: at most two original sessions per calendar month, including successful direct changes and reserved make-up benefits. 4\. Check that this original session has no previous adjustment or make-up benefit. 5\. Show the absence terms and the entitlement's expiry based on the original session date; obtain confirmation. 6\. Set the session to Absent, release its reservation, and create exactly one linked entitlement. 7\. Reserve one allowance for the original session's month. Do not consume it again when the entitlement is redeemed; UC16 changes this reservation to consumed on success. 8\. Send confirmation with the original session and entitlement expiry. |  |  |

| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Allowance Unavailable: Two original-session allowances in that contract/month are already reserved or consumed; do not grant another entitlement. EX-2 Notice Under 24 Hours: Reject the absence request. EX-3 Existing Benefit: Do not grant a second benefit for the same original session. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~15 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Notice and shared allowance: BR68, BR69, BR74, BR110. Absence and entitlement: BR70, BR71, BR72, BR73. Ownership and expiry: BR93, BR116, BR117. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Automatically releases valuable court inventory for single booking resale, optimizing facility occupancy. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The Customer understands the make-up session entitlement policy. |  |  |

**17 \<\<UC17 Request Member Cancellation\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC17 Request Member Cancellation |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | AnhTNHE181857 | **Date Created:** | 9/27/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Customer | **Secondary Actors:** | Facility Manager, Email Service (SendGrid), Banking Service (VietQR) |
| **Trigger:** | The Customer selects upcoming session(s) in a booking order and clicks "Request Cancellation". |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a Customer, I want to request cancellation of selected upcoming sessions in my booking order, with reservation release after approval and any refund handled separately. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The Customer owns the selected Planned, Booked sessions. PRE-2: Sessions have not started (BR114). PRE-3: No duplicate pending cancellation exists. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: Auto-approved requests cancel the selected sessions; manual requests remain Pending and keep reservations. POST-2: Only approved cancellation releases the relevant rights. POST-3: Any positive refund is recorded for approval/payout separately. Pending or zero-value refunds are not completed payments. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The Customer selects the session(s) to cancel in one order. 2\. Validate ownership, unstarted Booked sessions and no duplicate request. 3\. For each session, calculate h until start and net court fee actually paid after allocated discounts (BR106). Refund rates: h \>= 24: 80%; 12 \<= h \< 24: 50%; 6 \<= h \< 12: 30%; 0 \< h \< 6: 0%. 4\. Check the account's chain-wide calendar-month automatic cancellation allowance (BR83/107/115). From the third counted request, require Manager review; zero-refund approved cancellations still count. 5\. Display the affected sessions, refund breakdown and approval route. Obtain confirmation. 6\. If eligible for automatic approval, approve the request, mark selected sessions Cancelled and release their reservations. Otherwise store Pending and keep them Planned \+ Booked. 7\. Recompute the order status; do not cancel an entire order merely because one session was cancelled. 8\. For a positive refund, prioritize the original payment channel. Collect bank details only for a bank transfer; channel changes require Owner approval and customer agreement. 9\. Check cumulative successful, pending and requested refunds on the order for the Manager's 1,000,000 VND limit; escalate above it. Send request/approval confirmation, not proof of completed payout. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | AF-1 Reschedule: Invoke UC12 for an eligible session. AF-2 Manual Review: Keep reservations until UC19 approval. AF-3 Zero Refund: No bank details or payout are required. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Session Started: Reject prestart cancellation; use the authorized surrender process for remaining time. EX-2 Automatic Allowance Exhausted: Route to Manager review; do not release slots yet. EX-3 Invalid Ownership, Duplicate Request or Changed Session: Revalidate and reject invalid selections. Less than 2 hours before start is not itself a rejection reason; the refund is zero. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~20 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Refund rates and base: BR75, BR76, BR77, BR80, BR104, BR106. Approval count and pending reservations: BR83, BR85, BR107, BR108, BR115. Channels and evidence: BR86, BR89, BR102, BR103. Authority and refund limits: BR87, BR88, BR92. Ownership and cancellation eligibility: BR93, BR114. Used voucher preservation: BR42, BR52. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Refund completion requires valid payout evidence (BR89). |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The customer supplies valid beneficiary details only when an approved bank-transfer refund requires them. |  |  |

| **Primary Actor:** | Facility Manager | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | The Facility Manager accesses the pending cancellation list to evaluate a customer cancellation request |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows facility managers to verify and approve or reject guest cancellations and member cancellations that exceed automatic quotas |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The Facility Manager is authenticated with an active session. PRE-2: A pending cancellation request exists for a single or recurring booking in the manager's assigned branch facility |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The cancellation request status is updated to Approved or Rejected. POST-2: If approved, the court slot hold is released and a refund workflow (UC20) is triggered |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The Facility Manager navigates to the Pending Cancellations dashboard. 2\. The System displays the list of cancellation requests requiring manual review. 3\. The Facility Manager selects a request to view details (booking fee, cancellation reason, lead time h, automatic quota status).    4\. The Facility Manager clicks "Approve Cancellation".    5\. The System validates manager authority for the assigned branch. 6\. The System updates the request status to Approved, releases the court reservation hold, and calculates the eligible refund amount based on lead time rules.    7\. The System notifies the customer via email/notification and logs the review decision. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | ALT-1 Reject Cancellation Request: 1\. At step 4, the Facility Manager clicks "Reject Cancellation" and enters a reason.     2\. The System updates the request status to Rejected, retains the active booking hold, and notifies the customer. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Unauthorized Facility Access: 1\. The manager attempts to review a request for a facility branch outside their assigned scope. 2\. The System displays: "Access denied. You can only review requests for your assigned branch facility." |  |  |

| **Frequency of Use:** | \~15-20 times / day  |  |  |

| **Other Information:** | Review decisions are stored permanently in audit logs to prevent manager fraud. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Facility Managers perform daily checks on the pending cancellation queue. |  |  |

| **Assumptions:** | Customer is physically present at front desk to sign the receipt. |  |  |

**26 \<\<UC26 Reschedule Counter Booking\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC26 Reschedule Counter Booking |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | PhatLV | **Date Created:** | 19/10/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Staff   | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | A customer requests on-site rescheduling of an existing booking at the counter. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows staff to reschedule a customer's booking on-site upon request, subject to available courts and operational approval |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: Staff is authenticated with an active shift. PRE-2: Existing single booking exists and target replacement court slot is open. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: Original slot is released and new slot reservation is locked. POST-2: Price difference (if any) is settled at counter. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Staff looks up customer booking code or phone number. 2\. System presents booking details and eligible open slots. 3\. Customer selects new date, time, or court. 4\. System evaluates price difference (${G}_{m}-{G}_{c}$)  and applies rescheduling fee rules. 5\. Staff collects supplemental fee (if ${G}_{m}>{G}_{c}$ ) or proceeds if equal. 6\. Staff clicks "Confirm Counter Reschedule". 7\. System releases old slot, commits new slot, and issues updated booking ticket. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Late On-Site Reschedule Requires Manager Approval: 1\. Reschedule request occurs within restricted lead-time window (h \< 2h). 2\. System prompts for Facility Manager authorization override before permitting schedule swap. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~5-10 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | • BR81 (Rescheduling Supplement): The supplemental fee when rescheduling equals $\max\limits_{}({G}_{m}-{G}_{c},0)$ , where${G}_{c}$  is old post-voucher fee and ${G}_{m}$  is new schedule fee. • BR82 (Lower Price Refund Exclusion): A new schedule fee lower than the previous booking price does not generate any refund credit. • BR157 (Counter Rescheduling Exception): Only Facility Manager is authorized to approve on-site reschedule exceptions if quota/lead-time rules require override. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Protects peak time slot availability while allowing flexible customer service at counter. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Price differentials follow standard pricing policies without applying new promotional vouchers. |  |  |

**33 \<\<UC33 Check Out Booking\>\>**

| **Trigger:** | Customer finishes their court session and approaches the front desk to settle accounts.   |  |  |
| **Description:** | Finalizes settlement when the session concludes: sums court, retail, rental, overtime fees and damage compensation, offsets allocated prepayments and security deposits, and collects any remaining balance without re-charging paid court fees.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: Front-desk Staff is authenticated with an active shift. PRE-2: Court session is checked in and all rented equipment has been recorded as returned (UC32).   |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: Final settlement payment is collected and booking status updated to Completed. POST-2: Security deposit balance is returned to customer and physical receipt is issued. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Staff opens Check-Out screen for the court session. 2\. System computes net settlement obligation by summing court fee, retail, services, rental fee, extension, overtime, and damage compensation, then subtracting prepayments.    3\. System calculates applied deposit and remaining due balance.   4\. Staff informs customer of remaining balance and collects payment (Cash or VietQR).    5\. System records payment, returns remaining deposit balance, and marks booking status as Completed.    6\. System generates itemized final receipt (UC34)   |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Unreturned Rental Equipment: 1\. System detects unreturned rental items attached to session. 2\. System blocks checkout and prompts staff: "Must record equipment return (UC32) before final settlement." |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~80-120 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | • BR150 (Settlement Obligation): Net settlement sums all deliverables minus online prepayments. • BR152 (Remaining Collection Amount): Remaining due at counter equals net settlement minus applied deposit. • BR153 (Deposit Return Amount): Returned deposit equals initial deposit minus applied deposit and withheld dispute amount. • BR155 (Collection Completion Requirement): Session can only be completed when all due balances are paid. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Concludes operational lifecycle for single/recurring court sessions.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Customer settles remaining charges using front-desk payment channels. |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: Staff is logged into an active shift. PRE-2: All pending counter check-out transactions for the shift have been finalized.   |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: Physical cash counts by denomination are saved into the draft shift reconciliation record. POST-2: Total physical cash sum is calculated for variance checking. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Staff opens the Shift Closure screen and selects "Count Closing Cash".    2\. System displays a denomination input breakdown table (500k, 200k, 100k, 50k, 20k, 10k VND bills).    3\. Staff counts physical cash in the drawer and enters bill quantities for each denomination.    4\. System automatically calculates line subtotals and the grand total physical cash amount. 5\. Staff verifies total cash count and clicks "Save Closing Cash Count". 6\. System stores physical cash records and proceeds to shift reconciliation (UC37).  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Negative or Invalid Quantities: 1\. Staff enters negative bill quantities or non-numeric values. 2\. System displays error: "Invalid count. Bill quantities must be non-negative integers." |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have   |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~2-4 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | • BR163 (Payment Channel Classification): Physical cash must be strictly separated from electronic/VNPay/VietQR channel records during count verification. • Cash count entry is strictly mandatory before system reconciliation calculations can be generated. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Prevents manual counting math errors by providing automated denomination summation. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Staff physically recounts drawer cash prior to form submission. |  |  |

**48 \<\<UC48 Deactivate Staff Account\>\>**

|  |  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **UC ID and Name:** | **UC48 Deactivate Staff Account** |  |  |
| **Created By:** | PhuPDHE191603 | **Date Created:** | **21/10/2026** |
| **Primary Actor:** | **Facility Manager** | **Secondary Actors:** | **None** |
| **Trigger:** | **The Facility Manager selects "Deactivate Account" for a staff member in the branch staff directory upon resignation, termination, or transfer.** |  |  |
| **Description:** | **As a Facility Manager, I want to deactivate a staff account within my assigned branch, so that their system access is immediately revoked while preserving all historical operational and audit records.** |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1: The Facility Manager is authenticated and authorized for their assigned branch facility (BR100, BR207). PRE-2: The target Staff account exists, belongs to the same branch, and currently has status** Active **or** Locked**. PRE-3: The target Staff member does not have an active, unclosed work shift (**Shift.status \!= OPEN**, BR193).** |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1: The target Staff account status transitions to** Inactive **without physical deletion (BR209). POST-2: All active JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, and counter sessions for the staff account are immediately revoked (BR210). POST-3: Future scheduled shifts for the deactivated staff member are unassigned, and an audit log is recorded.** |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\. The Facility Manager navigates to the "Staff Management" module of their assigned branch. 2\. The System displays the list of branch staff accounts. 3\. The Facility Manager selects an active Staff account and clicks "Deactivate Account". 4\. The System checks for any active open shift (**Shift.status \= OPEN**) held by the selected staff member. 5\. The System prompts the Facility Manager to enter a mandatory deactivation reason (e.g., Resigned, Transferred) and confirm the action. 6\. The Facility Manager enters the reason and confirms deactivation. 7\. The System updates the account status to** Inactive **while preserving all historical transactions, receipts, and Z-Report records (BR209). 8\. The System immediately invalidates all active authentication sessions and refresh tokens of that staff account (BR210). 9\. The System records the deactivation audit log and displays a success notification.** |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Cancel Deactivation: 1\. At Step 5, the Facility Manager clicks "Cancel". 2\. The System aborts the operation and keeps the Staff account unchanged.** |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Staff Has Active Open Shift: 1\. At Step 4, the System detects that the staff member currently has an open counter shift. 2\. The System blocks deactivation and displays: "Cannot deactivate staff while an open shift is active. Please close and reconcile the shift first." EX-2 Unauthorized Branch Scope: 1\. The target staff account belongs to another branch facility (BR100). 2\. The System denies the request and logs an unauthorized access attempt.** |  |  |
| **Priority:** | **High, Must Have** |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | **\~1–3 times / month / branch** |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR100 (Manager Facility Scope): Facility Manager can only manage staff assigned to their branch. • BR193 (Staff Open Shift Limit): Active open shifts must be reconciled before account deactivation. • BR207 (Staff Deactivation Authority): Facility Manager is authorized to deactivate branch staff accounts. • BR209 (Account History Retention): Deactivating an account preserves all historical transaction and audit logs. • BR210 (Immediate Revocation): Deactivation immediately revokes all access tokens and terminates active sessions. • BR250, BR254: Inactive accounts cannot log in or self-service reset passwords.** |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | **Session revocation is enforced immediately via Redis token blocklist / token version increment.** |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | **Physical handover of keys and counter assets is completed offline according to branch HR procedures.** |  |  |

**49 \<\<UC49 View Court Occupancy\>\>**

|  |  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **UC ID and Name:** | **UC49 View Court Occupancy** |  |  |
| **Created By:** | PhupPD | **Date Created:** | **21/10/2026** |
| **Primary Actor:** | **Facility Manager** | **Secondary Actors:** | **None** |
| **Trigger:** | **The Facility Manager opens the "Court Occupancy Report" dashboard or changes report filter criteria.** |  |  |
| **Description:** | **As a Facility Manager, I want to view visual analytics and detailed metrics on court utilization and occupancy rates across sports and time periods at my branch, so that I can evaluate peak vs. off-peak performance.** |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1: The Facility Manager is authenticated and assigned to an active branch facility (BR100).** |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1: Branch court utilization ratios, peak/off-peak breakdowns, and court-by-court occupancy charts are displayed for the selected period.** |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\. The Facility Manager selects "Court Occupancy" from the branch analytics menu. 2\. The System defaults the filter to the current week for the manager's assigned branch. 3\. The Facility Manager selects filter parameters: Date Range, Sport Type (Badminton, Pickleball, Table Tennis), Court, and Time Period (All, Peak 17:00–22:00, Off-Peak). 4\. The System queries** Court**,** BookingSession**, and** CourtMaintenance **records within the selected timeframe for the branch. 5\. The System calculates total available bookable minutes (operating hours minus closures and maintenance windows) and total actual used court minutes (BR216). 6\. The System computes the Utilization Ratio \=** (Actual Used Minutes / Available Bookable Minutes) × 100% **(BR216). 7\. The System renders summary KPI cards, a heatmap by hour/day-of-week, and a tabular breakdown per court.** |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Reset Filters: 1\. The Facility Manager clicks "Reset" to return to the default current-week view across all sports in the branch.** |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Invalid Date Range: 1\. The selected start date is later than the end date. 2\. The System highlights the date fields and prompts the manager to select a valid interval. EX-2 No Booking Activity: 1\. No sessions occurred within the selected filter window. 2\. The System displays 0% utilization along with available bookable hours.** |  |  |
| **Priority:** | **Medium, Should Have** |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | **\~10–15 times / week / branch** |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR27 (Peak Period Definition): Peak hours are** \[17:00, 22:00) **on all days; all other operating hours are off-peak. • BR100 (Manager Facility Scope): Data is strictly scoped to the manager's assigned branch. • BR216 (Utilization Ratio): Court utilization ratio equals total court minutes actually used divided by total available bookable minutes after excluding closures and maintenance.** |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | **Dashboard queries use read-optimized indexes on** (facility\_id, start\_time, status) **to render within 2 seconds.** |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | **Court opening hours and maintenance blocks are accurately maintained in the system.** |  |  |

| **Created By:** | PhuPD | **Date Created:** | **21/10/2026** |
| **Primary Actor:** | **Facility Manager** | **Secondary Actors:** | **None** |
| **Trigger:** | **The Facility Manager navigates to the "Branch Revenue Report" screen or applies date/category filters.** |  |  |
| **Description:** | **As a Facility Manager, I want to view daily, weekly, and monthly revenue summaries for my branch categorized by court rental, retail sales, equipment rentals, and surcharges, so that I can track financial performance accurately.** |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1: The Facility Manager is authenticated and assigned to an active branch facility (BR100).** |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1: Recognized branch revenue, payment channel breakdowns, and separate tracking of deposits and unserved prepayments are displayed.** |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\. The Facility Manager opens the "Branch Revenue" dashboard. 2\. The System loads the default revenue summary for the current month at the manager's assigned branch. 3\. The Facility Manager selects desired filters: Time Granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Custom Date Range), Revenue Stream (Court Fees, Retail Consumables, Equipment Rentals, Overtime/Damage Compensation), and Payment Channel (Cash, VNPay, VietQR). 4\. The System retrieves settled** Invoice**,** InvoiceDetail**,** Payment**,** Refund**, and completed** BookingSession **/** ServiceOrder **records for the branch. 5\. The System calculates recognized management revenue strictly from delivered court sessions and handed-over goods/services, while separating security deposits and unserved advance prepayments into distinct liability columns (BR217). 6\. Where cost data is available for retail goods, the System calculates Gross Operating Profit \=** Net Revenue − Direct COGS **(BR218). 7\. The System displays revenue trend charts, category distribution pies, and detailed tabular summaries.** |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Drill Down by Shift or Date: 1\. The Facility Manager clicks on a specific date row. 2\. The System displays the breakdown of shifts and settled invoices recorded on that date.** |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 No Revenue Records in Period: 1\. No completed services or sales exist in the selected timeframe. 2\. The System displays zero-value KPI cards and an empty table state.** |  |  |
| **Priority:** | **High, Must Have** |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | **\~15–20 times / week / branch** |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR50 (Currency Rounding): Financial line items are rounded** HALF\_UP **to integer VND. • BR100 (Manager Facility Scope): Restricted strictly to the manager's assigned facility. • BR163 (Payment Channel Classification): Cash Flow is categorized by Cash, VNPay, and VietQR. • BR217 (Management Revenue Recognition): Revenue is recognized when service is delivered or goods are handed over; deposits and unserved prepayments are tracked separately. • BR218 (Gross Profit Scope): Gross operating profit equals net revenue minus direct cost of goods sold and must not be mislabeled as net profit.** |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | **Supports BO-2 and BO-3 operational tracking at the branch level.** |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | **Counter checkouts and Z-Report shift reconciliations are performed on schedule.** |  |  |

| **Trigger:** | The Court Owner selects "Register New Facility" in the Chain Administration portal. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows the Court Owner to register a new branch facility into the CourtChain network, specifying venue name, full physical address, geographical coordinates, standard operating hours, amenity descriptions, and primary contact details. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1:** The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR232, BR237, BR239). **PRE-2:** The proposed facility name and location do not duplicate an existing active facility in the chain. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1:** A new Facility record is created in the database with status "Active". **POST-2:** Operating schedule boundaries and time slot generation templates are initialized for the new branch. **POST-3:** An administrative audit log is created recording the registration action (BR247). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\.** The Court Owner navigates to "Chain Administration" \-\> "Facilities" and clicks "Add Facility". **2\.** The System presents the Facility Registration form (Facility Name, Address, City/District, Hotline Phone, Email, Operating Hours: Opening Time, Closing Time, Time Slot Granularity, Amenities: Parking, Shower, Pro-shop, Wi-Fi). **3\.** The Court Owner enters the facility profile information and submits the form. **4\.** The System validates all required fields, verifies opening time is strictly before closing time, checks phone/email formats, and ensures facility name uniqueness. **5\.** The System persists the new Facility entity with status "Active" and initializes operating configuration. **6\.** The System generates an administrative audit log entry per BR247. **7\.** The System displays a success message: "Facility registered successfully. You may now register courts and assign a Facility Manager." |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Immediately Add Courts:** Upon successful registration, the Court Owner clicks "Register Courts" to transition directly to UC53. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Duplicate Facility Name:** 1\. A facility with the same name already exists in the chain. 2\. The System rejects the submission and prompts the Court Owner to enter a distinct facility name. **EX-2 Invalid Operating Hours:** 1\. Closing time is earlier than opening time or duration is less than 4 hours. 2\. The System displays: "Closing time must be at least 4 hours after opening time." |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~1–2 times / quarter |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR234 (Facility Closure Eligibility):** Facility operational boundaries govern court availability and booking slot generations. **• BR235 (Court Facility Membership):** Every future sports court created must belong strictly to exactly one registered facility branch. **• BR246 (Master Record History Retention):** Branch facility records cannot be physically deleted; history is preserved indefinitely for auditing. **• BR247 (Catalog Audit Accountability):** Creating a facility branch records actor ID, timestamp, and metadata in admin logs. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Once registered, court units (UC53) and pricing policies (UC55) can be attached to the venue. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The Court Owner has legal and operational ownership of the physical premises. |  |  |
