**55 \<\<UC55 Create Court Pricing Policy\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC55 Create Court Pricing Policy |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | MinhHT | **Date Created:** | 21/10/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Court Owner | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | The Court Owner selects "Create Pricing Policy" in the Chain Administration portal. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows the Court Owner to create hourly court rental pricing policies defining standard rates, peak-hour surcharges (17:00–22:00), weekend rates, and recurring booking discount structures for a facility or sport type. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1:** The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR232). **PRE-2:** Target facility branches and sport categories exist in the system. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1:** A new CourtPrice policy version is persisted with an effective start date (BR244, BR245). **POST-2:** Peak-hour pricing enforces the minimum 1.20x multiplier floor over standard rates (BR233). **POST-3:** An audit log entry is written (BR247). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\.** The Court Owner navigates to "Pricing Management" \-\> "Court Pricing" and clicks "Create Policy". **2\.** The System presents the Pricing Policy Form (Policy Name, Scope: Facility-wide or Chain-wide, Sport Category, Regular Hourly Rate, Peak-Hour Hourly Rate, Weekend Hourly Rate, Recurring Contract Discount Rate, Effective Start Date). **3\.** The Court Owner inputs rates, schedules peak time window (17:00–22:00), and sets a future effective date. **4\.** The Court Owner clicks "Publish Policy". **5\.** The System validates that: all rates are positive (\> 0); peak-hour rate is \>= 1.20x regular rate (BR233); effective start date does not overlap an identical active policy version (BR244); effective date is not retroactive (BR245). **6\.** The System saves the CourtPrice policy version with status "Scheduled" (or "Active" if effective immediately). **7\.** The System logs the pricing creation in admin audit logs (BR247). **8\.** The System displays a confirmation alert: "Court pricing policy created successfully." |  |  |

## 

| Alternative Flows: | AF-1 Chain-Wide Policy Deployment: The Court Owner selects "Apply to All Branches", and the System links the policy as default across all chain venues. |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | ----- | ----- |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Peak Price Floor Violation:** 1\. Peak rate entered is less than 1.20x standard rate. 2\. The System rejects the submission and displays: "Peak-hour rate must be at least 1.20 times the regular rate per BR233." **EX-2 Retroactive Date:** 1\. Effective start date is set in the past. 2\. The System displays: "Effective date cannot be in the past per BR245." |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~2–4 times / year |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR232 (Pricing Policy Authority):** Only the Court Owner holds authority to issue, revise, or retire court pricing policies. **• BR233 (Peak Price Floor):** Peak-hour court rental pricing must be greater than or equal to 1.20 times the standard hourly rate. **• BR244 (Pricing Period Uniqueness):** Pricing versions sharing the same scope, sport, and slot type must have strictly disjoint date intervals. **• BR245 (Price Nonretroactivity):** Effective start date cannot be retroactive. **• BR246, BR247.**  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Peak hours default to 17:00–22:00 on weekdays and all-day on weekends. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Existing confirmed bookings locked their rental rates at time of reservation. |  |  |

**56 \<\<UC56 Revise Court Pricing Policy\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC56 Revise Court Pricing Policy |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | MinhHT | **Date Created:** | 21/10/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Court Owner | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | The Court Owner selects "Revise Policy" on an active court pricing policy. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Permits the Court Owner to update court rental price rates by publishing a new pricing policy version with a future effective date, strictly maintaining existing bookings at their locked price. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1:** The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR232). **PRE-2:** An existing active CourtPrice policy is selected for revision. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1:** A new version of the CourtPrice entity is created with future effective date (BR244, BR245). **POST-2:** The predecessor policy's effective end date is updated to align seamlessly with the new start date without gaps or overlaps. **POST-3:** All existing confirmed bookings remain locked at historical price rates (BR245). **POST-4:** An audit log is recorded per BR247. |  |  |

## 

| Normal Flow: | 1\. The Court Owner navigates to "Pricing Management" and selects "Revise" on an existing policy. 2\. The System clones current rate structures into a new version form and prompts for revised rates and mandatory Effective Start Date. 3\. The Court Owner updates rate figures, enters business justification, and submits the revision. 4\. The System verifies that effective start date is in the future (BR245), checks the 1.20x peak price rule (BR233), and verifies non-overlapping periods (BR244). 5\. The System creates the new CourtPrice version and sets the end date of the previous version to (Effective Start Date \- 1 second). 6\. The System logs the price revision with before/after rate comparisons and business rationale (BR247). 7\. The System notifies the Court Owner: "Pricing policy revised successfully. New rates will take effect on \[Effective Date\]." |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | ----- | ----- |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Immediate Rate Adjustment:** Effective date is current date/time; new rates apply immediately only to newly created bookings. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Validation Failure:** 1\. New peak rate violates 1.20x multiplier floor. 2\. System flags violation and prevents save. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~1–3 times / year |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR232 (Pricing Policy Authority), BR233 (Peak Price Floor).**  **• BR244 (Pricing Period Uniqueness):** Disjoint date intervals enforced. **• BR245 (Price Nonretroactivity):** Newly published rates cannot alter historical bookings. **• BR246, BR247.**  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Ensures price stability and transparent customer expectations. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Customers who booked prior to the revision retain their original confirmed price. |  |  |

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1: The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR101). PRE-2: The target** Voucher **campaign exists and is currently in** Active **or** Scheduled **status.** |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1: The voucher campaign status is updated to** Inactive **(retired) without physical deletion (BR246). POST-2: New voucher applications at checkout are blocked immediately. POST-3: Any voucher discount currently held within a valid 420-second checkout window remains protected until that hold settles or expires (BR66). POST-4: An administrative audit log with business rationale is recorded (BR247).** |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\. The Court Owner navigates to the "Voucher Campaigns" management screen (UC79). 2\. The Court Owner selects an active or scheduled campaign and clicks "Deactivate Campaign". 3\. The System displays current campaign metrics (total redemptions, consumed budget, and count of currently held checkout locks) and prompts for a mandatory deactivation rationale. 4\. The Court Owner inputs the business rationale and confirms deactivation. 5\. The System updates the campaign status to** Inactive **and records the effective deactivation timestamp. 6\. The System preserves existing valid 420-second checkout holds that already locked this voucher (BR66), while blocking any new checkout attempts from applying the code. 7\. The System writes an entry to the admin audit log with actor, timestamp, before/after state, and rationale (BR247), then displays a confirmation message.** |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Cancel Action: 1\. At Step 4, the Court Owner cancels the confirmation dialog. 2\. The campaign remains active.** |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Campaign Already Inactive or Expired: 1\. The selected campaign is already deactivated or past its end date. 2\. The System disables the action and informs the Court Owner that the campaign is no longer active. EX-2 Missing Rationale: 1\. The Court Owner submits without entering a business rationale (BR247). 2\. The System prompts the owner to provide a valid reason.** |  |  |
| **Priority:** | **Medium, Should Have** |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | **\~2–5 times / month** |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR65, BR66 (Held Voucher Protection): A validly held voucher discount is preserved until the 420-second hold expires even if the campaign is paused/deactivated. • BR246 (Master Record History Retention): Voucher campaigns cannot be physically deleted; full redemption history is preserved. • BR247 (Catalog Audit Accountability): Every modification by the Court Owner must record actor, timestamp, before/after values, and rationale.** |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | **Immediate cache invalidation ensures the voucher code is rejected on new checkouts within milliseconds.** |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | **The Court Owner has verified marketing or budget reasons for stopping the promotion early.** |  |  |

**62 \<\<UC62 View Chain Performance\>\>**

|  |  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **UC ID and Name:** | **UC62 View Chain Performance** |  |  |
| **Created By:** | PhuPD | **Date Created:** | **21/10/2026** |
| **Primary Actor:** | **Court Owner** | **Secondary Actors:** | **None** |
| **Trigger:** | **The Court Owner opens the "Chain Executive Dashboard" or adjusts chain-wide comparison filters.** |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1: The Court Owner is authenticated with chain-wide administrative privileges (BR101).** |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1: Consolidated chain KPIs, multi-branch revenue/occupancy comparison charts, and operational health metrics are displayed.** |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\. The Court Owner accesses the "Chain Performance" executive dashboard. 2\. The System aggregates data across all branch facilities for the default period (Current Month). 3\. The Court Owner optionally filters by Date Range, Selected Branches, Sport Category, or Booking Type (Single, Recurring, Walk-in). 4\. The System computes chain-wide and per-branch metrics: • Recognized Net Revenue and Gross Operating Profit (**Net Revenue − Direct COGS**, BR217, BR218). • Unserved Prepayments and Active Rental Deposits tracked separately (BR217). • Overall and Peak/Off-Peak Court Utilization Ratios (BR216). • No-Show Rate and Cancellation/Refund Totals. 5\. The System renders comparative bar charts across branches, time-series revenue trends, and a branch ranking table. 6\. The Court Owner can click any branch row to inspect detailed branch metrics.** |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Export Executive Summary: 1\. The Court Owner clicks "Export Financial Report" from the dashboard. 2\. The System invokes UC64 — Export Financial Report.** |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 Empty Filter Selection: 1\. No branches or valid dates are selected. 2\. The System prompts the owner to select at least one branch and a valid date interval.** |  |  |
| **Priority:** | **High, Must Have** |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | **\~20–30 times / week** |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR101 (Owner Chain Scope): Court Owner has chain-wide visibility across all facilities. • BR216 (Utilization Ratio): Used minutes divided by available bookable minutes (excluding closures and maintenance). • BR217 (Management Revenue Recognition): Recognizes delivered services/goods; separates deposits and unserved prepayments. • BR218 (Gross Profit Scope): Gross operating profit equals net revenue minus direct COGS when sufficient data exists.** |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | **Directly supports Business Objectives BO-1, BO-2, and BO-3 on the Court Owner Executive Dashboard.** |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | **All branch transactions are synchronized in the central database.** |  |  |

**63 \<\<UC63 View Chain Inventory\>\>**

|  |  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **UC ID and Name:** | **UC63 View Chain Inventory** |  |  |
| **Created By:** | PhuPDHE191603 | **Date Created:** | **21/10/2026** |
| **Primary Actor:** | **Court Owner** | **Secondary Actors:** | **None** |
| **Trigger:** | **The Court Owner selects "Chain Inventory" from the administration menu.** |  |  |
| **Description:** | **As a Court Owner, I want to view cross-branch inventory balances, available stock, quarantined stock, in-transit transfer quantities, and stocktake variance indicators across all facilities, so that I can identify surpluses, shortages, and approve stock transfers.** |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **PRE-1: The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR101).** |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **POST-1: Cross-branch inventory matrix, stock valuation, in-transit quantities, and low-stock alerts are displayed.** |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **1\. The Court Owner navigates to the "Chain Inventory" overview. 2\. The System queries** Product**,** Facility**,** StockDocument**, and** StockDetail **records across all branches. 3\. For each branch SKU, the System calculates and displays: • Physical On-Hand Stock, Held Order Reservations, and Quarantined Stock. • Available Stock \=** On-Hand − Held Reservations − Quarantined **(BR169). • In-Transit Stock currently dispatched between branches but not yet accepted (BR229). • Moving Average Cost valuation and latest Stocktake Variance Ratio (BR215). 4\. The Court Owner filters or searches by Branch, Item Category (Retail Sale vs. Rental Equipment), Stock Status (**IN\_STOCK**,** LOW\_STOCK**,** OUT\_OF\_STOCK**), or Pending Transfers. 5\. The System highlights branches with low stock alongside branches with surplus stock to assist inter-branch transfer decisions (UC66).** |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **AF-1 Review Pending Stock Transfers: 1\. The Court Owner clicks on a pending transfer alert or in-transit indicator. 2\. The System navigates to UC66 — Decide Stock Transfer.** |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **EX-1 No Matching SKUs: 1\. Filter criteria match no inventory records. 2\. The System displays an empty state and allows filter reset.** |  |  |
| **Priority:** | **Medium, Should Have** |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | **\~10–15 times / week** |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | **• BR101 (Owner Chain Scope): Full visibility into stock, costs, and suppliers across all facilities. • BR168, BR169 (Available Inventory): Available inventory equals physical on-hand minus validly held reservations minus quarantined stock. • BR215 (Inventory Variance Ratio): Evaluated using moving average cost. • BR229 (Transit Stock Classification): Dispatched unaccepted goods are classified as in-transit and not counted as available stock at either facility.** |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | **Provides the analytical basis for approving inter-branch transfers (BR226) and high-variance stocktakes (BR214).** |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | **Branch managers record goods receipts, dispatches, and weekly stocktakes accurately.** |  |  |

Load the account's single assigned role and applicable facility scope; do not restore revoked permissions. 5\. Issue the configured access and refresh tokens, store them using the defined secure cookie policy and update the login timestamp. 6\. Redirect only to an authorized destination for that role and scope. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | AF-1 Forgot Password (Extension Point): 1\. At Step 1, the user clicks "Forgot password?". 2\. The System invokes UC72 — Recover Password. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Invalid Credentials: Show a generic failure; issue no session. EX-2 Locked or Inactive: Reject login and direct the user to management. EX-3 Email Not Verified: Deny login until verification succeeds. EX-4 Requested Page Not Authorized: Deny that page without granting additional permissions. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~500 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Login restrictions: BR220, BR250, BR254. Role and facility scope: BR204, BR95, BR100, BR101. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Authentication API response latency \< 400ms. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The user remembers their registered Email and Password accurately. |  |  |

 

**71 \<\<UC71 Log In With Google\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC71 Log In With Google |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | AnhTNHE181857 | **Date Created:** | 9/27/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Guest, Customer | **Secondary Actors:** | Google Authentication Service (Google OAuth) |
| **Trigger:** | The user clicks "Continue with Google" on the login or registration modal. |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a Customer, I want to sign in with a verified Google identity while keeping existing account access restrictions and secure account linking. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The user possesses an active Google account. PRE-2: Google OAuth 2.0 API credentials are configured in CourtChain. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The Google identity and verified email are validated. POST-2: Create an Active Customer only for a new eligible identity, or link an existing Customer after explicit re-authentication. POST-3: Issue a session only if the CourtChain account is Active and authorized. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The user selects Continue with Google and authorizes access. 2\. Complete the OAuth exchange and validate the returned identity and verified email. 3\. If no matching account exists, create an Active Customer with emailVerified \= true. 4\. If the identity is already linked, retrieve the existing account. 5\. If only the email matches an unlinked Customer account, require explicit re-authentication of that CourtChain account before linking. Do not link automatically or merge internal-role accounts. 6\. Check CourtChain status Active and current permissions. Google authentication must not unlock or reactivate an account. 7\. Issue a session only after all checks succeed and redirect to an authorized page. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Consent Cancelled: Return to Login without a session. EX-2 Invalid Identity or Unverified Google Email: Reject sign-in. EX-3 Existing Account Link: Require explicit re-authentication; cancel or failure leaves the account unlinked. EX-4 Locked, Inactive or Ineligible Account: Deny sign-in; do not create a duplicate account or change its role. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High, Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~250 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Email and explicit linking: BR208, BR220, BR253. Role and account access: BR204, BR250. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Complies strictly with OpenID Connect (OIDC) core specifications. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Google Identity servers are accessible without network blocking. |  |  |

**72 \<\<UC72 Recover Password\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC72 Recover Password |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | AnhTNHE181857 | **Date Created:** | 9/27/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Account Holder | **Secondary Actors:** | Email Service (SendGrid) |
| **Trigger:** | The user clicks "Forgot password?" on the Login form. |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a user who forgot their password, I want to request a secure password reset link sent to my email, so that I can set a new password and regain access to my account. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The recovery page is accessible. PRE-2: The user can submit an email. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: An eligible account receives a single-use reset link valid for 15 minutes. POST-2: After valid token and new-password confirmation, the password is securely updated and the token consumed. POST-3: Role, verification and account status are unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The user submits an email on Forgot Password. 2\. Check its format, account existence and recovery eligibility; Inactive accounts cannot self-service reset (BR254). 3\. For an eligible account, send a single-use reset link valid for 15 minutes. 4\. Always show the same generic request acknowledgment. 5\. The user opens the link. Validate its account binding, expiry, unused status and current recovery eligibility. 6\. Show New Password and Confirm Password; validate the minimum length and matching values. 7\. Store the new password securely and consume the reset token together. 8\. Show confirmation and return to Login. Do not create a session automatically or change role, email verification, Locked or Inactive status. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | AF-1 Return to Login: 1\. At Step 2, the user recalls their password and clicks "Back to Login". 2\. The System navigates back to UC70 — Log In With Password. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Unknown or Ineligible Account: Show the generic acknowledgment; send no reset link. EX-2 Expired, Invalid or Used Token: Reject reset and allow a new eligible request. EX-3 Password Too Short or Confirmation Mismatch: Show validation errors without consuming a valid token. EX-4 Account Becomes Ineligible: Reject completion without restoring access. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~20 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Password validation: BR203. Recovery and access restrictions: BR254, BR250. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Reset link format: /reset-password?token=... with HMAC-SHA256 signature. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | SendGrid transactional email infrastructure operates with deliverability latency \< 30 seconds. |  |  |

**74 \<\<UC74 Change Password\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC74 Change Password |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | AnhTNHE181857 | **Date Created:** | 9/27/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | User | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | The account holder selects "Change Password". |  |  |
| **Description:** | As an account holder, I want to change my password using my current credential and revoke sessions on other devices. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The account holder is authenticated and authorized. PRE-2: The account has an existing password credential. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The new password hash is stored in database using BCrypt. POST-2: All existing active sessions and refresh tokens on other devices are revoked. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The account holder accesses Account Settings and clicks "Change Password". 2\. The System displays the password update form (Current Password, New Password, Confirm New Password). 3\. The account holder fills in required credentials and clicks "Update Password". 4\. The System verifies the current password hash with BCrypt. If mismatched, shows error. 5\. The System validates new password complexity: Minimum 6 characters (BR203), strictly distinct from current password (BR252), and identical to confirmation field. 6\. The System cryptographically hashes the new password with BCrypt (Salt Rounds \>= 10\) and persists it in the database. 7\. The System revokes all active sessions on other devices and generates a fresh session token. 8\. The System displays a confirmation alert notifying that the password was updated successfully. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | None. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Current Password Incorrect: Reject the change. EX-2 New Password Equals Current: Reject under BR252. EX-3 New Password Too Short: Require at least 6 characters under BR203. EX-4 Confirmation Mismatch: Require matching new-password values; do not save a change. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~10 times / day |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Password validation: BR203, BR252. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Session revocation ensures compromised devices are immediately disconnected. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The account holder knows the current password. |  |  |

(Login username, email, and assigned branch are displayed as read-only per BR248). **3\.** The Court Owner modifies contact details and clicks "Save Changes". **4\.** The System validates phone formats and ensures required fields are populated. **5\.** The System updates the Manager profile record in the database. **6\.** The System logs the update in the admin audit trail (BR247). **7\.** The System displays a confirmation message: "Manager profile updated successfully." |  |  |

**85 \<\<UC85 Deactivate Inventory Item\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC85 Deactivate Inventory Item |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | PhuPD | **Date Created:** | 21/10/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Court Owner | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | The Court Owner selects "Deactivate Item" for an active SKU at a designated branch facility in the Inventory Catalog. |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a Court Owner, I want to retire an inventory item (SKU) at a designated branch facility so that it cannot be added to new retail sales or rental orders, while preserving historical records and allowing pending order lines, active equipment rentals, and stock reconciliations to finish. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR239). PRE-2: The target Product (SKU) exists at the specified branch facility and has status Active. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The SKU status at the designated branch transitions to Inactive (retired) without altering physical or recorded stock quantities (BR221) and without physical deletion (BR246). POST-2: The retired SKU is immediately blocked from being added to new retail sales, new rental transactions, or advance service preferences (BR182). POST-3: Existing confirmed order lines, unreturned equipment rentals, financial settlements, and warehouse stock adjustments remain operable until resolved (BR183). POST-4: An administrative audit log with business rationale is recorded (BR247). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The Court Owner views the Inventory Catalog (UC83) for a branch and selects "Deactivate Item" on an active SKU. 2\. The System checks and displays current operational obligations for that SKU at the branch: physical on-hand stock, undelivered confirmed order lines, active unreturned rental items, and pending stock transfers. 3\. The System informs the Court Owner that retiring the SKU blocks new sales/rentals immediately (BR182) while existing obligations continue to completion (BR183), and prompts for a mandatory deactivation rationale (BR247). 4\. The Court Owner inputs the business rationale and confirms deactivation. 5\. The System updates the Product status to Inactive at that branch without modifying recorded stock balances (BR221) and preserves its unique SKU code (BR240, BR246). 6\. The System logs the change in the admin audit trail (actor, timestamp, before/after state, rationale per BR247) and displays a confirmation message. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | AF-1 Reactivate Retired SKU Later: 1\. If the Court Owner later wishes to sell/rent the item again, they can reactivate it via UC84 — Update Inventory Item. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 SKU Already Inactive: 1\. The target SKU is already in Inactive status. 2\. The System blocks duplicate deactivation. EX-2 Missing Rationale: 1\. The Court Owner submits without entering a business rationale (BR247). 2\. The System prompts for a valid explanation. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~2–5 times / month |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | • BR182 (Inactive SKU Eligibility): A retired SKU cannot be added to new retail sales or rental transactions from the effective time of retirement. • BR183 (Inactive SKU Existing Obligations): Retired SKUs must still fulfill existing confirmed order lines, equipment returns, financial settlements, and warehouse adjustments. • BR221 (Inventory Catalog Stock Separation): Retiring a SKU must not directly alter physical or recorded stock quantities. • BR239, BR240, BR246, BR247. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Scoped strictly to the selected branch facility; identically named items at other branches are unaffected. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Physical disposal or transfer of remaining stock on hand is handled separately via stock adjustments (UC45) or transfers (UC65). |  |  |

**88 \<\<UC88 Deactivate Facility\>\>**

| UC ID and Name: | UC88 Deactivate Facility |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | PhuPD | **Date Created:** | 21/10/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Court Owner | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Trigger:** | The Court Owner selects "Deactivate Facility" on an active branch facility record in Facility Management. |  |  |
| **Description:** | As a Court Owner, I want to deactivate a branch facility after verifying that all active sessions and future booking commitments have been completed or resolved, so that the branch is safely retired without breaching customer commitments while preserving historical records. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | PRE-1: The Court Owner is authenticated with chain administration privileges (BR101). PRE-2: The target Facility exists and currently has status Active. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | POST-1: The Facility status and its underlying Court statuses transition to Inactive without physical deletion (BR246). POST-2: The facility is removed from the public booking portal and map (UC1, UC2, UC3) and stops accepting any new bookings. POST-3: All historical bookings, invoices, shifts, and inventory records are preserved, and an audit log is recorded (BR246, BR247). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. The Court Owner opens Facility Management (UC75), selects an active branch facility, and clicks "Deactivate Facility". 2\. The System performs a comprehensive commitment check on the facility: • Active ongoing or future confirmed BookingSession records (Planned, CheckedIn, or active Holding). • Active RecurringBooking contracts with unresolved future sessions. • Open counter work shifts (Shift.status \= OPEN) or pending unapproved refunds. 3\. If zero unresolved commitments exist (BR222, BR234), the System prompts the Court Owner to enter a mandatory business rationale and confirm facility deactivation. 4\. The Court Owner enters the rationale and confirms. 5\. The System updates the Facility status (and its child courts) to Inactive, revoking public booking visibility while preserving all historical data (BR246). 6\. The System records the administrative audit log (actor, timestamp, before/after values, rationale per BR247) and displays a confirmation alert. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | AF-1 Place Maintenance Block While Resolving Future Bookings: 1\. If the owner wants to stop new bookings immediately while resolving existing future bookings, they first block the courts via UC39 and resolve affected bookings via UC40 before executing UC88. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | EX-1 Unresolved Active or Future Bookings Exist (BR222, BR234): 1\. At Step 2, the System detects active sessions or unresolved future single/recurring bookings at the facility. 2\. The System blocks deactivation and displays: "Cannot deactivate facility with active or unresolved future bookings. Please complete or resolve all affected customer bookings (via UC40) first." EX-2 Open Shift Exists: 1\. A reception counter at the facility has an open shift. 2\. The System blocks deactivation until all shifts at the branch are closed and approved. |  |  |
| **Priority:** | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | \~1–2 times / year |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | • BR222 (Facility Retirement Eligibility): A facility branch can only stop accepting new bookings after all active sessions and future service commitments have been completed or handled per facility-fault policies. • BR234 (Facility Closure Eligibility): A branch facility with active unresolved future bookings cannot be deactivated. • BR246 (Master Record History Retention): Facilities cannot be physically deleted; full history is preserved. • BR247 (Catalog Audit Accountability): Records actor, timestamp, before/after state, and business rationale. |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Prevents customer service breaches by enforcing a strict zero-unresolved-booking gate before shutdown. |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | All branch physical assets and remaining inventory are reconciled by management prior to closure. |  |  |

The System validates whether the selected court has any active checkout holds, ongoing CheckedIn sessions, or future Planned \+ Booked single or recurring sessions (BR223). 3\. The System rejects the deactivation request and displays the count of conflicting bookings that must be resolved via UC40 before the court can be deactivated. |  |  |
