Pending → AwaitingPayment when price check requires payment. AwaitingPayment → Applied when payment succeeds; otherwise → Rejected when payment fails or times out. |

### *III.3.7 MakeUpRequest*![][image287]

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a customer entitlement or request to redeem a make-up session for a previously reported absence on a recurring contract |
| Key business attributes | Request ID, entitlement code, issue date, expiration date, target slot details, status.   |
| Business identity | Unique entitlement ID linked to a recurring contract absence. |
| Status / lifecycle | Initial State → Pending when report absent is submitted. Pending → Available when quota check is valid, or Pending → Rejected when request is over quota. Available → Redeemed when used within 30 days; otherwise → Expired when 30 days timeout occurs. |

### 

### *III.3.8 Voucher*![][image288]

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a promotional discount voucher code issued under a marketing campaign for court bookings |
| Key business attributes | Voucher code, discount value, start date, expiration date, usage limit, status |
| Business identity | Unique voucher code linked to a campaign |
| Status / lifecycle | Initial State → Scheduled when voucher is created. Scheduled → Active when start date arrives, or Scheduled → Inactive when disabled. Active → Inactive when disabled by admin, or Active → Expired when end date arrives. |

### 

### *III.3.9 Invoice*

![][image289]

### 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a financial billing document and payment receipt generated for booking fees |
| Key business attributes | Invoice ID, invoice number, issue date, total amount, payment method, payment status |
| Business identity | Unique invoice number linked to a booking transaction |
| Status / lifecycle | Initial State → Unpaid when invoice is issued. Unpaid → Paid when full payment is received. Unpaid → PartiallyPaid when partial payment is made. PartiallyPaid → Paid when remaining balance is paid |

### 

### *III.3.10 Payment*  *![][image290]*

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a monetary transaction initiated to collect payment for court bookings, service orders, walk-in reservations, or recurring contract installments across supported channels. |
| Key business attributes | Payment ID, booking ID, invoice ID, payment channel (VNPay, VietQR, Cash), transaction reference (vnp\_TxnRef), payment amount, payment status (Pending, Succeeded, Failed), transaction timestamp, failure reason. |
| Business identity | Each payment has a unique transaction reference and belongs to one booking or service order. Once recorded, payment success or failure is immutable. A late payment received after slot hold expiration is marked Succeeded but does not resurrect the expired booking; instead, it triggers an automated full refund per BR60. Payment records are never transitioned to 'Refunded'; refund transactions are tracked independently via Refund and RefundPayment entities. |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes at Pending upon payment intent creation and redirection to the payment gateway or cashier prompt. Transitions to Succeeded upon receiving verified payment gateway callback (valid HMAC checksum) or front-desk cash collection confirmation. Transitions to Failed if the gateway returns an explicit failure/cancellation callback, user aborts payment, or the payment window expires without confirmation. Pending payments awaiting callback remain Pending until a conclusive response is obtained to avoid double-charging. |

### 

### *III.3.11 Cancellation* *![][image291]*

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an administrative request to cancel one, multiple, or all sessions of a court booking, initiated by a member Customer, an anonymous Guest (via secure email link), or facility management due to court maintenance/unavailability. |
| Key business attributes | Cancellation ID, booking ID, requester type (Customer, Guest, Facility), request timestamp, cancellation reason, cancellation status (Pending, Approved, Rejected), reviewed by, review timestamp, isAutoApproved flag. |
| Business identity | Each cancellation request has a unique identifier tied to one booking. A pending cancellation request maintains existing court occupancy (BR85). No partial approval state exists at the header level; per-session cancellation outcomes are recorded in linked CancellationDetail lines. Customer cancellations within monthly quota (\<= 2 times/month) are automatically approved (BR83); Guest requests and quota-exceeded requests require manual Facility Manager review (BR84). |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes into Pending for requests requiring manual evaluation; initializes into or immediately transitions to Approved for eligible Customer requests within monthly quota . Transitions from Pending to Approved upon Facility Manager authorization. Transitions from Pending to Rejected if denied due to policy violation or insufficient notice. Approved cancellations release court occupancy for resale and trigger linked refund evaluation. |

### 

### *III.3.12 CancellationDetail* *![][image292]*

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an individual court booking session item included within a cancellation request, recording the cancellation outcome and providing the granular calculation base for refund eligibility for that specific slot. |
| Key business attributes | Cancellation detail ID, cancellation ID, booking session ID, original slot fee, allocated voucher discount, cancellation rate , calculated refund amount, detail status (Pending, Approved, Rejected). |
| Business identity | Each cancellation detail item has a unique identifier and is uniquely linked to one parent Cancellation request and one specific BookingSession. Line items do not undergo an independent approval workflow; their lifecycle strictly mirrors and synchronizes with the parent Cancellation header. An Approved detail indicates that the specific slot is cancelled, but does not imply that refund money has already been disbursed (BR89). |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes at Pending alongside the parent Cancellation request. Transitions from Pending to Approved when the parent Cancellation is approved, locking in the calculated refund base according to the tiered cancellation timeline (BR75, BR76, BR77, BR80). Transitions from Pending to Rejected when the parent Cancellation is rejected, preserving the original booking session without modification. Approved details provide the authoritative basis for creating linked Refund claims |

### 

### *III.3.13  Refund* *![][image293]*

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an authorized financial refund claim or entitlement granting the return of previously collected funds to a customer resulting from booking cancellation, facility interruption/maintenance, or late payment on an expired hold. |
| Key business attributes | Refund ID, booking ID, cancellation ID (if applicable), refund reason, refund amount, refund status (Pending, Approved, Rejected), approval authority level (Facility Manager \<= 1M VND / Court Owner \> 1M VND), approved by, approval timestamp. |
| Business identity | Each refund record has a unique identifier tied to an original payment receipt. Approved status signifies authorization to disburse funds, but does not mean money has been paid out (BR89). Actual payout execution is modeled independently via RefundPayment entities. Cumulative approved and pending refunds for a booking cannot exceed the originally collected amount (BR92). Facility Managers can approve refunds up to 1,000,000 VND cumulative (BR87); amounts exceeding this threshold must be escalated to the Court Owner (BR88). |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes at Pending upon refund entitlement generation. Transitions from Pending to Approved upon authorization by the Facility Manager (for cumulative amounts \<= 1,000,000 VND) or by the Court Owner (for amounts \> 1,000,000 VND). Transitions from Pending to Rejected if authorization is denied due to policy violation or exceeded collection limits. Approved refunds permit the creation and execution of linked RefundPayment transactions. Total refund amount is permanently capped by net collected funds. |

### 

### *III.3.14 RefundPayment![][image294]*

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an individual monetary disbursement transaction executing an approved refund claim through a specific financial payout channel  |
| Key business attributes | Refund payment ID, refund ID, payout channel , disbursed amount, payout transaction reference / bank slip number, proof attachment URL, status, executed by, execution timestamp, verified by. |
| Business identity | Each refund payment record has a unique payout transaction identifier tied to an approved Refund record. To prevent duplicate disbursements, a payout transaction entering Processing remains locked in that state until definitive success verification or explicit failure confirmation is received. A failed payout does not alter or invalidate the parent Refund approval; rather, a new RefundPayment attempt record is instantiated. Bank transfers must strictly originate from registered facility bank accounts (BR102), and cash refunds require sufficient cash in an active work shift drawer (BR129). |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes at Pending upon selecting a payout channel and preparing the disbursement voucher. Transitions from Pending to Processing when the payout request is dispatched to the payment gateway (VNPay refund API) or when cashier/manager begins disbursement. Transitions from Processing to Succeeded upon confirmed gateway transaction callback or verified physical payment proof attachment (bank receipt / signed cash voucher per BR89). Transitions from Processing to Failed upon gateway error callback, rejected bank transfer, or drawer transaction failure. Unresolved transactions remain Processing to prevent double-spending. |

### 

### *III.3.15.ServiceOrder*

![][image295]

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Purpose** | Represents a service and retail order at the facility, tracking the fulfillment of goods/services, payment settlement, and associated obligations regarding equipment rentals, security deposits, and disputes. |
| **Key business attributes** | Order code, customer ID / booking session reference, facility ID, order timestamp, total amount, payment status, operational status. |
| **Business identity** | Each order has a unique identifier, is linked to a specific customer or booking session/shift, and records retail items sold, items rented, and auxiliary services provided. |
| **Status / lifecycle** | **States:** Open, Completed, Cancelled.• Initial → Open.• Open → Completed: upon completion of goods/services fulfillment, full settlement of required payments, and final resolution of all related rentals, deposits, and disputes.• Open → Cancelled: upon valid cancellation where no pending goods/rental obligations or unsettled financial balances remain.*Note:* Order cancellation does not void obligations for items already delivered, payments collected, or rented goods not yet returned. |

### *III.3.19.Shift*

### *![][image299]*

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a shift at the facility, tracking its operational progress and the approval status of its financial/shift report.  |
| Key business attributes | Shift code, facility ID, staff in charge, scheduled start/end time, actual open/close time, operational status, reporting status.  |
| Business identity | Each shift has a unique code, belongs to a specific facility, and corresponds to a specific time window in a day, recording cash collections, reconciliations, and handovers.  |
| Status / lifecycle | **Operational:** Planned → Open upon valid shift opening; Open → Closed upon proper shift closing. **Reporting:** NotSubmitted → PendingApproval upon counting, reconciling, and submission; PendingApproval → Approved upon authorized confirmation. Remains in PendingApproval if basis for approval is insufficient (no Rejected/Reopen states added). Approved reports retain history; discrepancies are handled via adjustment records.  |

### *III.3.20.CourtPrice*

![][image300]

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Manages the validity lifecycle of pricing policies applied to court bookings across specific time slots and periods.  |
| Key business attributes | Price ID, facility/court ID, rate, effective date, end date, price status.  |
| Business identity | Each price record has a unique identifier linked to the system or court pricing schedule, ensuring that prices locked for previous transactions remain unchanged.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes as **Scheduled** or **Effective**.**Scheduled → Effective** when the effective date is reached.**Effective → Ended** upon reaching the end date or valid termination.If no end date is specified, it remains **Effective** until terminated. Prices locked for prior transactions are preserved.  |

### *III.3.21.ProductPrice*

![][image301]

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Manages the validity lifecycle of pricing versions applied to inventory products (selling, rental, and compensation prices) across branches or the system.  |
| Key business attributes | Price version ID, product ID, price type (Selling/Rental/Compensation), rate, effective date, end date, price status.  |
| Business identity | Each price record has a unique identifier. Selling, rental, and compensation prices act as business configuration classifications rather than lifecycle states.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes as **Scheduled** (future date) or **Effective** (active immediately).**Scheduled → Effective** when the effective date is reached.**Effective → Ended** upon reaching expiration or valid termination.If no end date is specified, it remains **Effective** until terminated. New price versions do not affect or alter locked transaction prices for prior orders.  |

### *III.3.22.InvoiceDetail*

![][image302]

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Manages the payment lifecycle and settlement status of individual line items within an invoice based on receivable amounts and valid payment allocations.  |
| Key business attributes | Invoice detail ID, invoice ID, item reference, receivable amount, allocated amount, remaining due, payment status (Unpaid, PartiallyPaid, Paid).  |
| Business identity | Each invoice line item has a unique identifier linked to collection obligations, ensuring successful payments are accurately allocated without exceeding the due amount.   |
| Status / lifecycle | Initializes as **Unpaid** if the full receivable amount is pending; initializes as **Paid** if the obligation is zero.**Unpaid → PartiallyPaid** when a partial payment is received.**Unpaid or PartiallyPaid → Paid** when full payment is successfully allocated.**PartiallyPaid → PartiallyPaid** when additional partial amounts are collected but remain insufficient for full settlement. Refunds do not clear collection history.  |

## IV.3.1 . Package Diagram {#iv.3.1-.-package-diagram}

![][image310]

***Package descriptions***

| No | Package | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **01** | WebClient | Provides graphical user interfaces (UI) for Players (Customers), Court Owners, and Facility Staff; responsible for rendering administrative dashboards, interactive court schedule grids, pricing schemes, and dispatching reservation and management requests to underlying business packages. |
| **02** | AuthModule | Manages identity and access control; handles member registration, email activation token workflows, password authentication, Google OAuth2 SSO token verification, and enforces Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) boundaries for Court Owners, Staff, and Customers. |
| **03** | CourtModule | Governs the catalog and operational lifecycle of sports courts across branches (Badminton, Pickleball, Table Tennis); enforces branch exclusivity and single-sport constraints, and ensures courts cannot be deactivated or scheduled for maintenance while having active bookings. |
| **04** | PricingModule | Configures and manages court pricing policy versions across regular, weekend, and peak-hour slots (17:00–22:00); enforces the minimum $1.20\times$ peak price floor and guarantees disjoint effective intervals with no retroactive rate modifications. |
| **05** | BookingModule | Orchestrates end-to-end court reservation workflows, slot availability lookups, locked-in price retention at checkout, online payment settlement confirmations, and QR code check-in e-ticket issuance. |
| **06** | PromotionModule | Manages promotional voucher campaigns; validates discount constraints including percentage or fixed amounts, expiration intervals, usage quotas, and minimum order spend thresholds. |
| **07** | AuditLogModule | Automatically logs immutable administrative audit records for all configuration actions performed by Court Owners (court registration/updates, pricing revisions, voucher releases), capturing actor IDs, timestamps, and before/after snapshot values. |
| **08** | Database | Serves as the centralized data persistence layer; persistently stores facility court catalogs, accounts, booking transactions, pricing versions, and administrative system audit trails. |

## IV.4 Implementation Class diagram {#iv.4-implementation-class-diagram}

### *IV.4.1 Implementation Class Diagram for the Identity & Access Management Component*

The Identity & Access Management Component (Major Feature 7 \- MF7) governs user account registration, email verification token workflows, password authentication, Google OAuth2 SSO token verification, self-service password recovery, profile maintenance, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). It is realized using AuthController, ProfileController, AuthService, ProfileService, TokenCacheService, MailService, TypeORM Account Entity, and Repository\<Account\>.

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **AuthController** | Presentation (Controller) | Handles public and authenticated HTTP endpoints for member registration, email activation, credential login, password recovery, and password changes (/api/v1/auth). | \- authService: AuthService (Injected business service) | \+ register(dto: RegisterDto): Promise\<ApiResponse\<RegisterResult\>\> \+ verifyEmail(token: string): Promise\<ApiResponse\<VerifyResult\>\> \+ login(dto: LoginDto, res: Response): Promise\<ApiResponse\<LoginResult\>\> \+ forgotPassword(dto: ForgotPasswordDto): Promise\<ApiResponse\<void\>\> \+ resetPassword(dto: ResetPasswordDto): Promise\<ApiResponse\<void\>\> \+ changePassword(user: AuthenticatedUser, dto: ChangePasswordDto): Promise\<ApiResponse\<void\>\> |
| **2** | **ProfileController** | Presentation (Controller) | Manages member profile retrieval and update endpoints (/api/v1/profile), secured by JwtAuthGuard. | \- profileService: ProfileService (Injected profile service) | \+ getProfile(user: AuthenticatedUser): Promise\<ApiResponse\<AccountProfileDto\>\> \+ updateProfile(user: AuthenticatedUser, dto: UpdateProfileDto): Promise\<ApiResponse\<AccountProfileDto\>\> |
| **3** | **AuthService** | Business Logic (Service) | Encapsulates core authentication logic, credential validation, bcrypt password hashing (Salt Rounds \= 10), JWT token signing, and state transitions. | \- accountRepo: Repository\<Account\> \- tokenCache: TokenCacheService \- mailService: MailService \- jwtService: JwtService | \+ register(dto: RegisterDto): Promise\<RegisterResult\> \+ verifyEmail(token: string): Promise\<VerifyResult\> \+ login(dto: LoginDto): Promise\<LoginResult\> \+ forgotPassword(dto: ForgotPasswordDto): Promise\<void\> \+ resetPassword(dto: ResetPasswordDto): Promise\<void\> \+ changePassword(userId: string, dto: ChangePasswordDto): Promise\<void\> \+ validateJwtPayload(payload: JwtPayload): Promise\<Account\> |
| **4** | **ProfileService** | Business Logic (Service) | Manages profile read/write domain operations and ensures contact snapshot consistency. | \- accountRepo: Repository\<Account\> | \+ getProfile(userId: string): Promise\<AccountProfileDto\> \+ updateProfile(userId: string, dto: UpdateProfileDto): Promise\<AccountProfileDto\> |
| **5** | **TokenCacheService** | Business Logic (Service) | High-speed ephemeral key-value store managing short-lived cryptographic tokens with automatic TTL expiration. | \- tokenStore: Map\<string, CacheEntry\> | \+ set(key: string, value: string, ttlSeconds: number): Promise\<void\> \+ get(key: string): Promise\<string \| null\> \+ del(key: string): Promise\<void\> |

### *IV.4.2 Implementation Class Diagram for the Court Booking Management Component*

The Court Booking Management Component (Major Feature 1 \- MF1) provides self-service badminton court discovery, interactive schedule grid rendering, 7-minute temporary distributed hold locking (via Redis Redlock), voucher discount redemption, online prepayment via VNPay, and automated booking session creation. It is realized using BookingController, BookingService, RedlockService, PaymentService, TypeORM Booking and BookingSession Entities, and Repositories.

**Figure IV.4-2. Implementation class diagram for the Court Booking Management component**

## IV.5 Database Design

### *IV.5.1 Database Management System Selection Rationale*

The CourtChain multi-branch sports venue management platform provides an enterprise Microsoft SQL Server (2019 / 2022\) database deployment option. This implementation adheres to the technical non-functional requirements (NFRs) specified in Table 3 of the project report:

·         **High-Performance Primary Keys (NEWSEQUENTIALID):** Primary keys utilize UNIQUEIDENTIFIER with DEFAULT NEWSEQUENTIALID(). Unlike random GUIDs generated by NEWID(), NEWSEQUENTIALID() generates sequentially ascending GUIDs that prevent B-Tree index page splitting and fragmentation, maximizing clustered index insert throughput.

·         **Zero Double-Booking Conflict Prevention via Scalar UDF:** To match PostgreSQL's range exclusion capability in T-SQL, conflict checking is implemented via an atomic deterministic function dbo.fn\_CheckCourtConflict(@court\_id, @start\_at, @end\_at, @session\_id). The function is bound directly into a table CHECK constraint on booking\_session, ensuring zero double-booking at the database engine level.

·         **Unicode String Storage & Temporal Integrity:** All textual fields are typed as NVARCHAR (supporting UTF-16 Vietnamese characters, customer names, addresses, and multi-branch notes). Temporal timestamps utilize DATETIMEOFFSET with SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(), preserving accurate UTC offset information across multi-timezone operations.

·         **Domain Status Enums Enforced via Declarative Check Constraints:** In conformance with T-SQL architectural standards, domain enum types are enforced declaratively using CHECK (\[column\] IN ('VAL1', 'VAL2', ...)) directly on the column definition, ensuring strict value domain integrity with zero table-join overhead.

**IV.5.2 Database Sub-Diagrams (7 Cluster Diagrams)**

The 35 database tables are partitioned into 7 logical sub-diagrams mirroring the 7 domain components:

**Sub-Diagram 1: Identity & Access Control**

Manages multi-role user credentials, Google OAuth tokens, and branch staffing assignments.

·         Included Tables: account

![][image313]

**Sub-Diagram 2: Facility & Court Infrastructure**

Defines venue branches, court sports surfaces, and scheduled repair outage blocks.

·         Included Tables: facility, court, court\_maintenance

![][image314]

**Sub-Diagram 3: Pricing & Promotion Policies**

Calculates dynamic time-of-day/weekend court fees and enforces voucher discount limits.

·         Included Tables: court\_price, voucher

![][image315]

**Sub-Diagram 4: Booking & Court Session Operations**

Coordinates single/recurring reservations, slot conflict exclusion, rescheduling, and player reviews.

·         Included Tables: booking, booking\_session, recurring\_booking, weekly\_schedule, booking\_change, make\_up\_request, review

![][image316]

**Sub-Diagram 5: Billing, Invoicing & Refunds**

Aggregates charges into immutable invoices, tracks VNPay/VietQR/Cash payments, and processes refunds.

·         Included Tables: invoice, invoice\_detail, payment, payment\_detail, cancellation, cancellation\_detail, refund, refund\_payment

![][image317]

**Sub-Diagram 6: Inventory, Services & Equipment Rentals**

Controls retail commodities, rental equipment tracking, security deposit movements, and goods receipts.

·         Included Tables: product, product\_price, stock\_document, stock\_detail, service\_order, service\_order\_detail, service\_request, rental, deposit\_transaction

![][image318]

**Sub-Diagram 7: POS Counters & Shift Cash Control**

Governs front-desk cash registers, opening floats, closing denomination counting, and manager Z-Reports.

·         Included Tables: counter, shift, cash\_count, cash\_count\_detail, cash\_transaction

![][image319]

| DDL Template — \[account\] \-- \[ACCOUNT\] — User accounts supporting 4-tier RBAC, Google OAuth 2.0 SSO, and facility quarantine \-- SRS Reference: Entity from SRS 4.1.1 (Account), DC-01 (Password Encryption), BR-01 (Role Boundary) \-- MS SQL Server: Enum values enforced via column CHECK constraint CREATE TABLE account ( 	account\_id      	UNIQUEIDENTIFIER	PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT NEWSEQUENTIALID(), 	facility\_id     	UNIQUEIDENTIFIER	NULL REFERENCES facility(facility\_id) ON DELETE NO ACTION, 	display\_name    	NVARCHAR(100)   	NOT NULL, 	email           	NVARCHAR(150)   	NOT NULL UNIQUE, 	phone           	NVARCHAR(20)    	NOT NULL UNIQUE, 	password\_hash   	NVARCHAR(255)   	NULL, 	role            	NVARCHAR(50)    	NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CUSTOMER' CHECK (role IN ('CUSTOMER', 'STAFF', 'FACILITY\_MANAGER', 'COURT\_OWNER')), 	email\_verified  	BIT             	NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 	status          	NVARCHAR(50)    	NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE', 'SUSPENDED', 'INACTIVE', 'PENDING')), 	created\_at      	DATETIMEOFFSET  	NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(), 	updated\_at      	DATETIMEOFFSET  	NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET() ); GO \-- Indexes — justify each one with the query pattern it supports CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX idx\_account\_email ON account(email);  \-- Login authentication and OAuth token verification CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX idx\_account\_phone ON account(phone);  \-- Front-desk customer lookup by phone number CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX idx\_account\_facility\_id ON account(facility\_id);  \-- Staff listing and multi-branch data isolation filtering GO |

**Table 10: weekly\_schedule — Weekly recurring day and time patterns utilized to batch-generate dated court sessions**

| DDL Template — \[weekly\_schedule\] \-- \[WEEKLY\_SCHEDULE\] — Weekly recurring day and time patterns utilized to batch-generate dated court sessions \-- SRS Reference: Entity from SRS 4.1.9 (WeeklySchedule), DC-10 (Minimum Duration), BR-10 (Schedule Rule) \-- MS SQL Server: Enum values enforced via column CHECK constraint CREATE TABLE weekly\_schedule ( 	schedule\_id     	UNIQUEIDENTIFIER	PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT NEWSEQUENTIALID(), 	recurring\_id    	UNIQUEIDENTIFIER	NOT NULL REFERENCES recurring\_booking(recurring\_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, 	court\_id        	UNIQUEIDENTIFIER	NOT NULL REFERENCES court(court\_id) ON DELETE NO ACTION, 	day\_of\_week     	NVARCHAR(50)    	NOT NULL CHECK (day\_of\_week IN ('MONDAY', 'TUESDAY', 'WEDNESDAY', 'THURSDAY', 'FRIDAY', 'SATURDAY', 'SUNDAY')), 	start\_time      	TIME            	NOT NULL, 	duration\_minutes	INT             	NOT NULL CHECK (duration\_minutes \>= 30),  \-- DC-10, 	created\_at      	DATETIMEOFFSET  	NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(), 	updated\_at      	DATETIMEOFFSET  	NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(), 	UNIQUE (recurring\_id, court\_id, day\_of\_week, start\_time)  \-- BR-10: Rule uniqueness per contract ); GO \-- Indexes — justify each one with the query pattern it supports CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX idx\_weekly\_schedule\_recurring ON weekly\_schedule(recurring\_id);  \-- Batch session generator query GO |

**Table 11: booking\_change — Customer requests to reschedule playing sessions to an alternate court or time window**

 \-- Session change audit trail CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX idx\_booking\_change\_quota ON booking\_change(session\_id, quota\_month);  \-- Enforce monthly free reschedule policy GO |

 \-- Branch accounting & uncollected accounts ledger GO |

**IV.5.4 Conflict Prevention UDF and Cross-Module Foreign Keys**

The conflict detection UDF and cross-module foreign key constraints are defined below:

| DDL Specification — T-SQL Function & Foreign Keys \-- Zero Double-Booking Constraint Function for MS SQL Server CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.fn\_CheckCourtConflict ( 	@court\_id UNIQUEIDENTIFIER, 	@start\_at DATETIMEOFFSET, 	@end\_at DATETIMEOFFSET, 	@session\_id UNIQUEIDENTIFIER ) RETURNS INT AS BEGIN 	DECLARE @conflict\_count INT; 	SELECT @conflict\_count \= COUNT(\*) 	FROM booking\_session 	WHERE court\_id \= @court\_id   	AND session\_id \<\> @session\_id   	AND reservation\_status NOT IN ('CANCELLED', 'NO\_SHOW')   	AND start\_at \< @end\_at   	AND end\_at \> @start\_at; 	RETURN @conflict\_count; END; GO \-- Cross-Module Foreign Keys: ALTER TABLE voucher ADD CONSTRAINT fk\_voucher\_session FOREIGN KEY (source\_session\_id) REFERENCES booking\_session(session\_id) ON DELETE SET NULL; ALTER TABLE invoice\_detail ADD CONSTRAINT fk\_invdetail\_service\_order FOREIGN KEY (service\_order\_id) REFERENCES service\_order(service\_order\_id) ON DELETE SET NULL; ALTER TABLE payment ADD CONSTRAINT fk\_payment\_shift FOREIGN KEY (shift\_id) REFERENCES shift(shift\_id) ON DELETE NO ACTION; ALTER TABLE refund\_payment ADD CONSTRAINT fk\_refundpay\_shift FOREIGN KEY (shift\_id) REFERENCES shift(shift\_id) ON DELETE NO ACTION; ALTER TABLE service\_order ADD CONSTRAINT fk\_serviceorder\_shift FOREIGN KEY (shift\_id) REFERENCES shift(shift\_id) ON DELETE NO ACTION; ALTER TABLE deposit\_transaction ADD CONSTRAINT fk\_deposittrans\_shift FOREIGN KEY (shift\_id) REFERENCES shift(shift\_id) ON DELETE NO ACTION; GO |
| :---- |

 

# **V. Implementation**

## ***V.1 Map Architecture to the Structure of the Project***

### *V.1.1 Overview of the Chosen Architecture*

The CourtChain badminton court management and operational chain platform implements a hybrid architectural paradigm combining a Client-Server 3-Tier Macro-Architecture with a Component-Based Layered Micro-Architecture (commonly designated in modern enterprise software engineering as Package-by-Feature with Internal Layering or Modular Monolith). This architecture establishes clean physical separation across presentation, application, and persistence infrastructure while enforcing robust modular boundaries and encapsulation within the Node.js backend codebase.

**1\. Macro-Architecture: Client-Server 3-Tier Physical Distribution**

The operational environment is partitioned into three autonomous tiers to enforce strict separation of concerns, infrastructure security, and horizontal scalability:

·        **Presentation Tier (Client Applications):** Built with React 18, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. The tier is divided into two tailored user workflows: (a) the Customer Web Portal, optimized for responsive self-service browsing, court availability heatmaps, slot reservations, and online payments; and (b) the Front-Desk POS & Management Dashboard, optimized for high-throughput counter check-ins via mobile camera QR scanning (\< 1.0s), walk-in bookings, equipment rentals, and shift cash balancing.

·         **Application Tier (Node.js Backend Server):** Implemented using Node.js (v20+ LTS), TypeScript, and the NestJS framework. Functions as the core business logic engine, hosting stateless RESTful APIs, enforcing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) via Passport-JWT and Guards, coordinating distributed locking for slot reservations using ioredis and Redlock, managing transactional integrity across multiple domain aggregates via TypeORM QueryRunner, and mediating third-party integrations (VNPay, VietQR, SendGrid).

·         **Data Tier (Persistence & Infrastructure):** Provides specialized persistent and in-memory data capabilities. PostgreSQL 16 serves as the primary ACID-compliant relational store housing the 35 domain entities. Redis 7 serves as the high-speed in-memory store for distributed reservation locks (7-minute TTL) and availability caching. MinIO / S3 Object Storage archives binary court gallery photos, generated PDF receipts, and e-ticket QR badges.

**2\. Micro-Architecture: Component-Based Layered Architecture (Modular Monolith)**

Rather than organizing the codebase horizontally into traditional global layers (which scatters domain logic across distant packages like src/controllers, src/services, and src/repositories), CourtChain adopts a Component-Based Modular Layered Architecture (Package-by-Feature with Internal Layering). In the Node.js/NestJS ecosystem, each business capability is encapsulated within an autonomous NestJS Module:

·         **identity:** User registration, authentication, RBAC authorization, staff provisioning, and manager assignment.

·         **facility:** Multi-branch facilities, court configurations, operating slots, and maintenance blocking.

·         **pricing:** Dynamic time-of-day/weekend court pricing policies and promotional voucher campaigns.

·         **booking:** Single reservations, recurring contracts, front-desk walk-in bookings, QR check-in validation, session rescheduling, cancellations, and make-up credits.

·         **billing:** Invoices, invoice details, VNPay/VietQR payment processing, refunds, and financial audit logs.

·         **inventory:** Retail products, equipment rental, stock replenishment documents, stock adjustments, and inter-branch transfers.

·         **shiftcash:** POS cash registers, cash handover shifts, denomination cash counts, variance logging, and manager Z-Report approvals.

·         **common:** Centralized cross-cutting infrastructure including global exception filters, standard REST response interceptors, JWT guards, and distributed locking helpers.

Within each domain module, a rigorous 3-layer architecture is implemented:

·         **Presentation / Web Layer (controllers, dto):** Exposes RESTful endpoints using NestJS @Controller decorators, handles HTTP serialization, enforces declarative validation via class-validator and ValidationPipe, and maps internal entities to external DTOs.

·         **Business Logic Layer (services):** Houses domain business logic, state machine transitions, validation rules, and transactional boundaries using @Injectable services and TypeORM QueryRunner.

·         **Data Persistence Layer (repositories, entities):** Encapsulates TypeORM custom repositories, entity definitions (@Entity), and database queries.

**3\. Strict Inter-Component Communication via Exported Service Interfaces**

To avoid cross-module coupling and spaghetti dependencies, direct access from one component to another's internal repositories or entities is strictly prohibited. When the Booking component requires facility operational hours or pricing calculations, it communicates exclusively via public service interfaces (e.g., IFacilityService, IPricingService) exported in the target module declaration (exports: \[FacilityService\]). This enforces the Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) and Interface Segregation Principle (ISP), guaranteeing complete domain encapsulation.

### *V.1.2 Architectural Selection Rationale and Fulfillment of Non-Functional Requirements*

The selection of the Component-Based Layered Architecture was guided by a rigorous evaluation against alternative architectural paradigms (pure package-by-layer monolithic architecture vs. fully distributed microservices) in the context of the Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs) specified in Table 3 of this document.

**Table V.1-1. Architectural Style Evaluation and Trade-off Matrix**

| Architectural Criterion | Naive Layered Architecture (Package-by-Layer) | Fully Distributed Microservices | Chosen: Component-Based Layered Architecture (NestJS) |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Domain Encapsulation | Low. Feature logic is fragmented horizontally across distant layers. | High. Isolated deployment units per domain. | High. Encapsulated in feature modules with private internal layers. |
| Operational Complexity | Very Low. Single deployment unit, straightforward debugging. | Very High. Requires service discovery, API gateway, circuit breakers, distributed tracing. | Low. Single deployable Node.js application, zero distributed networking overhead. |
| Transaction Integrity | High. Single database transaction manager. | Low. Requires complex distributed transactions (Saga pattern / 2PC). | High. Local ACID transactions across all 35 entities with guaranteed atomicity via TypeORM. |
| Team Development Velocity | Degrades rapidly as team members produce git merge conflicts across common folders. | High coordination overhead for interface contracts across independent repos. | High. Independent feature development within modular packages without collision. |
| Path to Future Scalability | Low. High refactoring cost required to decouple entangled dependencies. | Already decoupled, but introduces early latency and network overhead. | Optimal. Clean interface contracts enable frictionless extraction into SOA / microservices. |

The chosen architecture directly satisfies each of the system's core Non-Functional Requirements:

**1\. Maintainability and Portability (NFR \#6)**

·         **High Cohesion & Low Coupling:** By packaging controllers, services, repositories, and domain models together within domain modules (e.g., src/modules/booking), developers achieve high cognitive locality. Changes to booking validation, rescheduling rules, or cancellation workflows are strictly confined to the booking module without unexpected side effects in identity or shiftcash.

·         **Infrastructure Portability:** The entire Node.js backend is containerized using multi-stage Docker builds (node:20-alpine), ensuring reproducible execution across local development environments, continuous integration pipelines, and cloud staging/production servers.

**2\. Scalability and Architectural Evolvability (NFR \#2 & Section VI Alignment)**

·         **High Concurrency & Low Latency:** The asynchronous event-driven Node.js runtime combined with Redis connection pooling seamlessly handles ≥ 200 concurrent user sessions with sub-2.0s response latency.

·         **Multi-Branch Expansion:** The modular database tenancy design supports scaling up to 20 branch facilities, 200 courts, and 50 POS counters without architectural restructuring.

·         **Frictionless Microservice Migration:** As explored in Chapter VI (Applying Alternative Architecture Patterns), because modules interact strictly via exported service interfaces, high-load components such as booking or billing can be cleanly extracted into independent microservices or an SOA architecture with dynamic service discovery without rewriting internal domain logic.

**3\. Reliability, Availability and Concurrency Control (NFR \#4)**

·         **Atomic Distributed Slot Locking:** Court slot contention is managed at the business logic layer using ioredis and Redlock distributed locks (SET key value NX PX 420000\) with a strictly enforced 7-minute TTL. This prevents race conditions and eliminates double-booking before database transactions initiate.

·         **ACID Transactional Boundaries:** Multi-step operations—such as POS check-out involving invoice finalization, cash receipt creation, inventory consumption, and shift balance updates—are executed within atomic database transactions via TypeORM QueryRunner, guaranteeing ACID consistency.

·         **Idempotent Gateway Callbacks:** External payment webhooks (VNPay IPN) utilize cryptographically signed idempotency keys, guaranteeing that duplicate gateway callbacks cannot result in multiple charges or conflicting booking states.

**4\. Security and Multi-Tenant Isolation (NFR \#3)**

·         **Centralized Security Perimeter:** The common/guards module hosts JwtAuthGuard and RolesGuard, which extract and verify HMAC-SHA256 tokens and inject the authenticated UserPrincipal into the execution context before dispatching requests to controllers.

·         **Multi-Branch Data Quarantine:** Repositories and services enforce facility-level multi-tenant isolation, ensuring that Cashiers and Facility Managers are quarantined strictly to their assigned facility\_id.

·         **Financial Immutability & Audit Trails:** Approved shift Z-Reports and completed refund records are strictly read-only and permanently locked against modification or deletion.

**5\. Reusability and Testability (NFR \#1, NF-05)**

·         **Comprehensive Unit Testability:** Separating service interfaces from concrete implementations allows 100% isolated unit testing using Jest and NestJS Test.createTestingModule without booting database connections.

·         **Reusable Infrastructure Kernel:** Reusable utilities for dynamic VietQR payload generation, check-in QR ticket rendering, standard REST response wrappers (ApiResponse\<T\>), and business exception filters are centralized in the common kernel and shared across all modules.

# **VI. Applying Alternative Architecture Patterns** {#vi.-applying-alternative-architecture-patterns}

## ***VI.1 Applying Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) for Multi-Branch Operations***

### *VI.1.1 Problem Identification & Architectural Deficiencies of Current Monolith*

In Section V, the CourtChain platform was realized following a Client-Server 3-Tier Macro-Architecture combined with a Component-Based Layered Micro-Architecture (Modular Monolith). While this architectural pattern accelerated baseline development and streamlined local transactions using TypeORM QueryRunner, critical operational bottlenecks and architectural deficiencies emerge as CourtChain expands across 20+ branch facilities with hundreds of courts and high-concurrency booking rushes. Specifically, several Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs) defined in Chapter II (Table 3\) cannot be adequately supported by the current monolithic architecture:

• **Deficiency Against NF-02 (Scalability & Peak Traffic Surges):** In the current modular monolith, all domain modules (Identity, Facility, Pricing, Booking, Billing, Inventory, ShiftCash) execute inside a single Node.js runtime process sharing a single V8 JavaScript event loop and a single database connection pool. During morning slot releases (07:00–08:30) and flash voucher promotions, hundreds of customers concurrently query availability matrices, acquire Redis Redlock keys, and redirect to payment gateways. This intense CPU and asynchronous I/O load locks the event loop and exhausts database connection pools. As a direct result, unrelated mission-critical counter operations at physical branches—such as front-desk staff scanning QR codes (\< 1.0s target) or processing physical walk-in cash payments—suffer severe latency spikes (\> 5.0s) or request timeouts. Furthermore, horizontal scaling requires replicating the entire application container, duplicating idle modules (e.g., shift management, facility setup) and unnecessarily multiplying database connection overhead.

• **Deficiency Against NF-04 (Reliability, Availability & Blast Radius Containment):** In a monolithic process space, zero runtime failure isolation exists. An unhandled exception, severe memory leak, or CPU-intensive background job in a secondary module—such as a complex monthly PDF financial report generation in Billing or multi-branch inventory reconciliation in Inventory—triggers an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) kill by the operating system kernel. When the single Node.js process crashes, the entire application becomes unreachable. Front-desk staff across all 20 branch facilities are instantly paralyzed and unable to check in arriving players, process rental equipment, or balance cash drawers, turning a localized background job failure into a chain-wide operational shutdown.

• **Deficiency Against NF-06 / NF-05 (Modularity, Reusability & Autonomous Deployment Agility):** Domain logic is tightly bound to internal NestJS dependency injection tokens and monolithic TypeORM relational schemas. High-value business logic—such as the Dynamic Pricing Engine or Identity & Authentication Service—cannot be independently reused by third-party tournament aggregators, mobile self-service kiosks at branch entrances, or external corporate sports booking platforms without exposing the entire backend repository and database. Moreover, releasing a minor patch (e.g., updating VNPay HMAC-SHA512 checksum logic or tweaking rental equipment prices) requires rebuilding, regression testing, and redeploying the entire monolithic application, introducing unnecessary release friction and deployment risk.

### *VI.1.2 SOA-Based Redesign Solution*

To resolve these deficiencies, the CourtChain backend is redesigned using Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA), structuring system components into seven autonomous business services, an Edge API Gateway, and an Asynchronous Enterprise Event Bus. Each service is completely encapsulated with its own bounded context and isolated data store:

| Service Name | Bounded Context & Responsibilities | Autonomous Data Store | Inter-Service Communication |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **IAM & Auth Service (Port 8001\)** | User accounts, password encryption (bcrypt), Google OAuth2 SSO, stateless JWT token issuance, multi-tenant RBAC. | courtchain\_iam\_db (PostgreSQL) | Exposes gRPC/REST token validation endpoints to API Gateway and other services. |
| **Facility & Court Service (Port 8002\)** | Multi-branch locations, court layouts, operating schedules, maintenance slot blocking. | courtchain\_facility\_db (PostgreSQL) | Exposes query endpoints for court operational status and branch metadata. |
| **Dynamic Pricing Service (Port 8003\)** | Dynamic time-of-day tariffs, weekend multipliers, promotional voucher campaigns, discount validation engine. | courtchain\_pricing\_db (PostgreSQL) \+ Redis Cache | Invoked synchronously by Booking Service via HTTP/gRPC for price quotes. |
| **Booking Core Service (Port 8004 \- Scaled)** | Slot availability matrix, 7-minute temporary hold locking, single/recurring reservations, QR check-in, rescheduling. | courtchain\_booking\_db (PostgreSQL) \+ Redis Cluster | Elastic horizontal autoscaling; publishes domain events (BookingCreated, BookingCancelled). |
| **Billing & Payment Service (Port 8005\)** | Invoice lifecycle, VNPay gateway redirect, VietQR image generation, idempotent IPN webhooks, automated refunds. | courtchain\_billing\_db (PostgreSQL) | Consumes BookingCreatedEvent; invokes VNPay API; publishes PaymentCapturedEvent. |
| **Inventory & POS Retail (Port 8006\)** | Front-desk retail merchandise sales, racket/shoe rental tracking, goods receipt documents, stocktake, branch transfers. | courtchain\_inventory\_db (PostgreSQL) | Consumes BookingCreatedEvent for equipment rental; exposes POS checkout APIs. |
| **Shift & Cash Service (Port 8007\)** | Cashier shifts, cash drawer balances, denomination counts, cash variance logging, manager Z-Report approvals. | courtchain\_shiftcash\_db (PostgreSQL) | Consumes PaymentCapturedEvent for cash transactions; enforces shift financial immutability. |

 

**Key Architectural Decoupling Mechanisms in CourtChain SOA:**

• **API Gateway Pattern:** The API Gateway (Kong / Traefik) serves as the unified reverse proxy entry point. It abstracts microservice locations from client applications, terminates TLS 1.3, authenticates JWT bearer tokens, enforces IP rate limiting against brute-force attacks, and routes requests according to URI path prefixes (/api/v1/bookings/\* \-\> Booking Service).

• **Event-Driven Architecture (EDA) & Saga Orchestration:** Cross-service business transactions (e.g., booking confirmation, invoice generation, payment receipt, and inventory rental hold) are decoupled using an asynchronous Enterprise Event Bus (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka). Instead of brittle, synchronous HTTP chains that fail if any downstream service is slow, the Booking Service emits a BookingCreatedDomainEvent. Downstream Billing and Inventory services consume this event independently. This ensures high availability and loose coupling adhering to the Choreography-based Saga Pattern.

• **Database-Per-Service (Bounded Context Persistence):** Direct cross-service database querying is strictly eliminated. Each microservice possesses its own isolated database schema or instance. If the Booking Service needs customer profile details or court specifications, it must query the respective service via defined API contracts or rely on cached denormalized read models.

### *VI.1.3 Supporting Diagrams for SOA Architecture*

#### ***VI.1.3.1 Deployment Diagram (SOA Architecture)***

The SOA Deployment Diagram illustrates how independent services are packaged into containerized runtimes (Docker containers / Kubernetes Pods), distributed across distinct host machines, connected via an internal virtual network, and backed by isolated databases and shared clustering infrastructure. Client requests from web browsers and POS terminals are routed through the Edge API Gateway Cluster, while inter-service messaging is coordinated via RabbitMQ and Redis clusters.

#### ***VI.1.3.2 Component Diagram (Independent Services & Interfaces)***

The Component Diagram details the autonomous microservices, their provided interfaces (Lollipop notation), required interfaces (Socket notation), and their integration through the Enterprise Event Bus. The Booking Service realizes IBookingServiceApi while consuming IFacilityServiceApi and IPricingServiceApi, publishing BookingCreatedEvent to RabbitMQ to notify Billing and Inventory.

#### ***VI.1.3.3 Updated Class Diagram (SOA Service Contracts, Proxies, and DTOs)***

In the refactored SOA codebase, direct service-to-service class references are replaced by Remote Service Client Proxies implementing segregated interfaces (e.g., HttpPricingServiceClient implementing IPricingServiceClient with circuit breaker fallback), strongly-typed Data Transfer Objects (DTOs), and domain event publishers (RabbitMQBookingEventPublisher).

 

## ***VI.2 Applying Service Discovery Pattern in the Service-Oriented Architecture***

### *VI.2.1 Problem & Requirement Analysis*

With the decomposition of the system into independent services, modern container orchestration platforms (such as Kubernetes, Docker Swarm, or AWS ECS) are utilized to host and scale the application instances. However, dynamic cloud environments introduce fundamental routing challenges governed by the Non-Functional Requirements defined in Chapter II:

• **Relevant Non-Functional Requirement (NF-02: Scalability & Elasticity):** NF-02 mandates that CourtChain support seamless multi-branch expansion (up to 20 branches, 200 courts, and 50 POS counters) and absorb sudden traffic surges during booking release windows. To meet these demands, high-throughput microservices such as Booking Core Service and Dynamic Pricing Service must scale horizontally from 2 to 10+ container instances (Pods) elastically during peak hours (07:00–09:00 and 17:00–21:00) and scale back down at night.

• **The Need for Service Discovery in Ephemeral Container Environments:** In containerized clusters, service pods are ephemeral. Pods are dynamically provisioned, terminated, or rescheduled across worker nodes during autoscaling or host maintenance. Each new pod is assigned an unpredictable private IP address (e.g., 10.244.1.15, 10.244.2.22). Traditional static approaches—such as hardcoding IP addresses in configuration files or manually editing reverse-proxy upstream directives—completely break down: manual reconfiguration is impossible at cloud speeds, configuration drift occurs, and dead pods continue receiving traffic, causing intermittent HTTP 502/504 errors that violate NF-04 (Reliability & 99.5% Availability). Therefore, an automated mechanism for dynamic service registration, health monitoring, and endpoint discovery is essential.

### *VI.2.2 Service Discovery-Based Solution*

To enable automated registration, dynamic routing, and automated self-healing, the Service Discovery Pattern is integrated into the CourtChain architecture. The solution comprises three core components: (1) a centralized, highly available Service Registry; (2) automated Service Registration with periodic heartbeat health checks; and (3) Dynamic Service Discovery & Load Balancing (both Server-Side via API Gateway Ingress and Client-Side via DynamicDiscoveryClientProxy).

| Evaluation Criteria | HashiCorp Consul (Selected Primary) | Netflix Eureka (Spring Cloud) | Kubernetes CoreDNS & Kube-Proxy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Architecture Model** | Distributed Raft Consensus; Client/Server Agent model. | Peer-to-peer replication; AP model (CAP Theorem). | Etcd-backed DNS server \+ Linux iptables / IPVS proxy. |
| **Protocol Support** | HTTP REST API, DNS interface, gRPC. | HTTP REST API (Java client optimized). | Standard DNS SRV/A records, Virtual ClusterIP. |
| **Health Checking** | Comprehensive: HTTP, TCP, Docker, gRPC, and TTL script probes natively supported. | Simple heartbeat check; slow eviction (up to 90s lag). | Pod readiness/liveness probes evaluated by Kubelet. |
| **Language Ecosystem** | Polyglot (First-class TypeScript, Node.js, Go, Python, Java). | Primarily optimized for JVM / Spring Boot. | Platform-native; completely agnostic of application language. |
| **Suitability for CourtChain** | Ideal: Ultra-fast failure detection (\< 5s), multi-branch datacenter support, direct NestJS Terminus integration. | Less suitable: Heavy Java dependencies; higher discovery latency. | Complementary: Utilized as the underlying container network discovery inside Kubernetes. |

 

**Selected CourtChain Discovery Workflow:**

• **1\. Boot & Registration:** Upon container initialization, the NestJS microservice boots its HTTP server, registers its Terminus health check indicators (database pool and Redis cache), and executes an automated registration request to the Consul cluster (POST /v1/agent/service/register).

• **2\. Periodic TTL Heartbeat:** The service's background agent transmits a heartbeat to Consul every 10 seconds. Consul also actively probes the /health/live endpoint.

• **3\. Dynamic Upstream Synchronization:** The API Gateway (Kong / Envoy) maintains a persistent Long-Polling Watch connection with Consul. When new booking service pods are spawned to absorb peak traffic, Consul pushes the updated IP catalog to the gateway within milliseconds.

• **4\. Load-Balanced Ingress:** External customer requests are dynamically balanced across active, healthy pods using Round Robin or Weighted Least Connections.

• **5\. Automated Self-Healing & Eviction:** If a pod crashes or experiences database lockup, two missed heartbeats (20s) cause Consul to flag its status as CRITICAL. The gateway immediately evicts the dead instance from its routing table, achieving 100% zero-traffic routing to failed nodes.
